textes.Les armoiries naissent en Europe occiden: Arms emerged in western Europe between about the 1130s and the 1170s; the shields credited to the first Capetians were attributed to them after the fact. The page “Héraldique française”, however, takes this story back to the 11th century.
textes.Aucune des pages consultées ne lui attri: None of the pages consulted credits him with arms.
textes.Le lis, emblème avant l'écu: The lily, an emblem before the shield
textes.Sous Louis VII, le lis devient un signe: Under Louis VII the lily became a sign of royalty in its own right: his seal shows him crowned with three lilies. Several clues suggest he bore fleur-de-lis arms as early as the Second Crusade (1147), but the only known image of the arms of France in the 12th century is a banner painted in the margin of a manuscript from Saint-Victor.
textes.Le semé est attesté au début du XIIIᵉ si: The semé is attested at the start of the 13th century; depending on the page, the first semé shield dates from 1209, 1211 or 1223.
textes.Blasonnement relevé sur les sceaux royau: Blazon taken from the royal seals (the corpus of Martine Dalas, cited by the Armorial). The Armorial also gives a “modern” reading, with the chains of Navarre; the page “Armoiries de la France” specifies that in the 14th century Navarre is not yet shown by chains.
textes.Le passage à trois lis est daté de 1376: The move to three lilies is dated to 1376 and credited to Charles V, who placed the kingdom under the invocation of the Trinity. Another passage gives 1375; the page “France (héraldique)” notes three-lily shields much earlier and makes Charles VI, after 1380, the first to bear them on his great seal.
textes.Le 13 août 1830, le roi fait graver les: On 13 August 1830 the King had the arms of his house engraved on the seal of State.
textes.Les pages ne décrivent pas la charge de: The pages do not describe the charge in the same way: tables of the Law for the Armorial des Capétiens, an open book reading “Charte de 1830” for the page Monarchie de Juillet, simply “the Charter or” for the page Armoiries de la France.
textes.Même blasonnement pour Napoléon Iᵉʳ et p: Same blazon for Napoleon I and for Napoleon III in the Armorial of the House of Bonaparte. The page “Armoiries de la France” blazons otherwise: an eagle rising, the head turned to sinister — and specifies that the official blazon does not mention the turned head.
textes.Armes d'Henri comme roi de Pologne, de 1: Arms of Henry as King of Poland, from 1573 to 1575; afterwards, the three lilies alone.
textes.Mille ans d'armes royales: A thousand years of royal arms
textes.D'Hugues Capet à Napoléon III, l'écu du: From Hugh Capet to Napoleon III, the sovereign's shield keeps changing its face: semé of lilies, three lilies, Navarre, eagle, Charter. Drag the timeline — the central shield follows the reign under the golden line; around it, each king adds his crown, his supporters, his collars, his arms as a prince and his motto.
textes.Son sceau montre déjà une couronne ornée: His seal already shows a crown decorated with three lilies — an emblem, not yet arms.
textes.Les armes qu'on lui prête comme comte de: The arms credited to him as Count of Vexin — a semé of lilies with a label ermine — were very probably composed long after him.
textes.Il use d'une bannière bleue fleurdelisée: He used a blue banner with gold fleurs-de-lis from 1191; the first attested semé shield is that of his son Louis, on a seal of 1211.
textes.La Liste des monarques de France lui don: The Liste des monarques de France already gives him the dimidiated France-Navarre; the Armorial des Capétiens describes this dimidiation only from Louis X.
textes.Prince, second fils de Philippe III: Prince, second son of Philip III
textes.Roi à sa naissance, il ne règne que cinq: King at birth, he reigned only five days.
textes.Comte d'Alençon, de Chartres et du Maine: Count of Alençon, Chartres and Maine
textes.L'image montre la variante à la bordure: The image shows the variant with the bordure gules.
textes.Charles VI fait du cerf ailé son emblème: Charles VI made the winged stag his favourite emblem, according to the Songe du vieil pèlerin by Philippe de Mézières.
textes.Tapisserie des Cerfs ailés, fin du XVᵉ s: Tapestry of the Winged Stags, late 15th century
textes.le cerf ailé, en support: the winged stag, as a supporter
textes.Il reprend le cerf ailé de son père comm: He took up his father's winged stag as the supporter of his arms, and gave them two angels as supporters.
textes.L'Armorial le range parmi les porteurs d: The Armorial lists him among the bearers of this quartering of Orléans and Milan, marked “citation needed”.
textes.Il use aussi de l'abeille et de la ruche: He also used the bee and the hive, with “Non utitur aculeo rex cui paremus”, and the winged stag as a supporter.
textes.Animal réputé se nourrir du feu. Les gra: An animal said to feed on fire. The spelling of the motto varies from one object to another.
textes.Blasonnement marqué « référence nécessai: Blazon marked “citation needed” in the Armorial.
textes.le croissant, souvent triple et entrelac: the crescent, often triple and interlaced
textes.Jusqu'à ce qu'il emplisse le monde entie: Until it fills the whole world
textes.Le croissant est aussi l'emblème de Dian: The crescent is also the emblem of Diana the huntress, used by Diane de Poitiers.
textes.Dauphin, roi d'Écosse par son mariage: Dauphin, King of Scots by marriage
He married Mary Stuart on 24 April 1558.
textes.La même liste lui donne aussi « Lumen re: The same list also gives him “Lumen rectis” (light lies in uprightness).
textes.Roi de Pologne quand il hérite de la Fra: King of Poland when he inherited France, he kept for a time the arms of Poland, with France overall.
textes.La Liste de devises royales en donne une: The Liste de devises royales gives a long form: “Manet ultima coelo donec totum compleat orbem”.
textes.Ses armes simples : écartelé de Navarre: His simple arms: quarterly Navarre and Bourbon (azure, three fleurs-de-lis or, a bend gules).
textes.L'une protège l'autre (la France et la N: One protects the other (France and Navarre)
textes.La Liste de devises royales traduit : «: The Liste de devises royales translates: “One protects the other two”.
textes.Les monstres aussi la connaîtront: The monsters too shall know it
textes.Les traductions varient d'une page à l'a: Translations vary from one page to another.
textes.Autres traductions : « à nul autre parei: Other translations: “like no other”, “alone against all”. The nickname “Sun King” is late: it goes back to the July Monarchy.
textes.Suspendu le 10 août 1792, il perd la cou: Suspended on 10 August 1792, he lost the crown on 21 September.
textes.Il fuit Paris dans la nuit du 20 mars 18: He fled Paris on the night of 20 March 1815, when Napoleon returned. The Armorial des Capétiens still gives the kings of the Restoration the France-Navarre impalement, borne “occasionally” according to the Commons page for it; other pages speak only of the lilies.
textes.Michel Popoff, cité par l'Armorial, blas: Michel Popoff, cited by the Armorial, blazons otherwise: quarterly France and Provence (azure, one fleur-de-lis or).
He returned to Paris on 8 July 1815.
textes.L'Armorial des Capétiens lui donne aussi: The Armorial des Capétiens also gives him the France-Navarre impalement; other pages speak only of the lilies.
textes.L'aigle est l'emblème impérial ; l'abeil: The eagle is the imperial emblem; the bee, proposed by Vivant Denon and Cambacérès, became his personal symbol and appeared at the coronation of 2 December 1804.
textes.Rentré à Paris le 20 mars 1815, il abdiq: Back in Paris on 20 March 1815, he abdicated on 22 June, four days after Waterloo.
textes.Désigné par l'abdication de son père, il: Named by his father's abdication, he was never proclaimed or recognised.
textes.Il rétablit l'abeille impériale, dans sa: He restored the imperial bee, in its traditional form with folded wings.
textes.Devenu roi, il garde d'abord ces armes s: Once king, he at first kept these arms under the royal crown.
textes.Des décrets de la Convention abolissent: Decrees of the Convention abolished the royal arms.
textes.Le sceau d'Hugues Capet montre une couro: The seal of Hugh Capet shows a crown decorated with three lilies: the lily is already a royal sign, but not yet a coat of arms.
textes.Les armoiries apparaissent en Europe occ: Arms appeared in western Europe between about the 1130s and the 1170s. Any shield credited to an earlier king is a late attribution.
textes.La page « Héraldique française » fait re: The page “Héraldique française” takes this story back to the 11th century.
textes.Au sacre de Philippe Auguste, le manteau: At the coronation of Philip Augustus, the royal mantle was probably already blue semé of gold lilies; the composition is certain by about 1200.
textes.Un sceau du prince Louis, futur Louis VI: A seal of Prince Louis, the future Louis VIII, bears the first attested shield semé of lilies.
textes.D'autres pages donnent 1209, ou 1223 ave: Other pages give 1209, or 1223 with a seal of Louis VIII once king.
textes.Rois de France et de Navarre, Louis X pu: As Kings of France and Navarre, Louis X and then his brothers dimidiated the semé of France with the escarbuncle of Navarre.
textes.Avec Philippe VI, premier Valois, l'écu: With Philip VI, the first Valois, the royal shield went back to the semé of France alone.
textes.Charles V réduit le semé à trois lis, po: Charles V reduced the semé to three lilies, to place the kingdom under the invocation of the Trinity.
textes.Un autre passage dit 1375 ; la page « Fr: Another passage says 1375; the page “France (héraldique)” finds three-lily shields as early as Louis VIII and sees Charles VI, after 1380, as the first to bear them on his great seal.
textes.Louis XI fonde l'ordre de Saint-Michel :: Louis XI founded the Order of Saint Michael: its collar henceforth surrounds the royal shield, held by two angels since Charles VII.
textes.Introduite par Louis XII, la couronne fe: Introduced by Louis XII, the closed crown became the rule with Francis I.
textes.Le collier du Saint-Esprit: The collar of the Holy Spirit
textes.Henri III crée l'ordre du Saint-Esprit ;: Henry III created the Order of the Holy Spirit; the kings very often display both collars around their arms.
textes.Roi de Navarre devenu roi de France, Hen: A King of Navarre turned King of France, Henry IV impaled the three lilies with the chains of Navarre; his successors kept this impalement.
textes.Le 19 juin 1790, l'Assemblée constituant: On 19 June 1790 the Constituent Assembly abolished the nobility and its signs; arms, regarded as signs of feudalism, fell with it. Decrees of the Convention then abolished the royal arms.
textes.D'autres pages datent la suppression de: Other pages date the abolition to 1789, or have the royal arms run until 1792.
textes.Napoléon prend pour armes une aigle d'or: Napoleon took as his arms a golden eagle on a field azure, inspired by the Roman eagle.
textes.La Restauration ramène les fleurs de lis: The Restoration brought back the fleurs-de-lis.
textes.Le 13 août 1830, Louis-Philippe fait met: On 13 August 1830 Louis Philippe had the arms of his house — France with a label argent — placed on the seal of State.
textes.Après les émeutes de février 1831, une o: After the riots of February 1831, an ordinance of 16 February replaced the arms of Orléans with a shield bearing the Charter of 1830.
textes.Le Second Empire reprend l'aigle de Napo: The Second Empire took up the eagle of Napoleon I, under the same blazon.
textes.Le semé sous la couronne ouverte: The semé under the open crown
textes.France et Navarre sous la couronne ouver: France and Navarre under the open crown
textes.La page date ce mi-parti de 1305, quand: The page dates this dimidiation to 1305, when the future Louis X became King of Navarre.
textes.Les trois lis sous la couronne ouverte: The three lilies under the open crown
textes.Anges tenants et collier de Saint-Michel: Angel supporters and the collar of Saint Michael
textes.collier de l'ordre de Saint-Michel: collar of the Order of Saint Michael
textes.deux anges tenants, vêtus d'argent: two angel supporters, clad in argent
textes.Charles VII donne aux armes deux anges p: Charles VII gave the arms two angels as supporters, as eldest daughter of the Church; his son Louis XI founded the Order of Saint Michael in 1469.
textes.Louis XII introduit la couronne fermée a: Louis XII introduced the closed crown at the start of the 16th century; Francis I made it the normal usage.
textes.colliers des ordres de Saint-Michel et d: collars of the Orders of Saint Michael and the Holy Spirit
textes.Henri III crée l'ordre du Saint-Esprit e: Henry III created the Order of the Holy Spirit in 1578; his successors very often show both collars.
textes.Les grandes armes de France et de Navarr: The great arms of France and Navarre
textes.écus de France et de Navarre accolés: shields of France and Navarre side by side
textes.heaume d'or doublé de gueules, lambrequi: golden helm lined with gules, mantling azure and or
textes.colliers de Saint-Michel et du Saint-Esp: collars of Saint Michael and the Holy Spirit
textes.deux anges aux dalmatiques de France et: two angels in dalmatics of France and Navarre, each holding a banner
textes.manteau d'azur fleurdelisé doublé d'herm: azure mantle with fleurs-de-lis, lined with ermine, under a pavilion
textes.cri « Montjoie Saint-Denis », oriflamme,: war cry “Montjoie Saint-Denis”, oriflamme, motto “Lilia non laborant neque nent”
textes.Manteau, pavillon, oriflamme, cri et dev: Mantle, pavilion, oriflamme, cry and motto were added in the 17th and 18th centuries. The two shields side by side amount to an impalement.
textes.L'aigle sous la couronne impériale: The eagle under the imperial crown
textes.grand collier de la Légion d'honneur: grand collar of the Legion of Honour
textes.La tendance est aux seules armes de Fran: The tendency is towards the arms of France alone, but the Bourbons also took up those of Navarre.
textes.cordon de la Légion d'honneur: ribbon of the Legion of Honour
textes.sceptre et main de justice en sautoir: sceptre and hand of justice in saltire
textes.L'ordonnance du 13 août 1830 fixe ainsi: The ordinance of 13 August 1830 fixes the seal of State in this form.
textes.La Charte, sceptre et drapeaux tricolore: The Charter, sceptre and tricolour flags
textes.Les fleurs de lis disparaissent aussi de: The fleurs-de-lis also disappear from the crown, according to the Armorial des Capétiens.
textes.L'aigle du Second Empire: The eagle of the Second Empire
textes.Mêmes armes qu'au Premier Empire ; seuls: Same arms as in the First Empire; only the outer ornaments change.
textes.Couronne royale fleurdelisée fermée, int: Closed royal crown with fleurs-de-lis, introduced by Louis XII, made general by Francis I.
textes.Couronne royale fermée, d'où les fleurs: Closed royal crown, from which the fleurs-de-lis disappear.
textes.Charles VII donne aux armes deux anges p: Charles VII gave the arms two angels as supporters, as eldest daughter of the Church; they remain on the great arms until the Revolution. The exact date of their appearance is not given.
textes.Le cerf ailé, emblème de prédilection de: The winged stag, favourite emblem of Charles VI, was chosen as supporter of the arms by Charles VII.
textes.Louis XII reprend à son tour le cerf ail: Louis XII in turn took up the winged stag as supporter of his arms.
textes.Collier de l'ordre de Saint-Michel, fond: Collar of the Order of Saint Michael, founded by Louis XI in 1469.
textes.Colliers des ordres de Saint-Michel et d: Collars of the Orders of Saint Michael and the Holy Spirit; the Order of the Holy Spirit was created by Henry III in 1578.
Grand collar of the Legion of Honour.
textes.Colliers des ordres de Saint-Michel et d: Collars of the Orders of Saint Michael and the Holy Spirit.
Ribbon of the Legion of Honour.
textes.Manteau d'azur fleurdelisé doublé d'herm: Azure mantle with fleurs-de-lis, lined with ermine, pavilion, oriflamme, war cry “Montjoie Saint-Denis” and motto “Lilia non laborant neque nent”: added in the 17th and 18th centuries, with no more precise date.
textes.Les trois léopards qu'on prête aux rois: The three lions credited to the Norman kings and the first Plantagenets were attributed to them after the fact — by Matthew Paris as early as the 1250s. The heraldic system is not yet fixed: the shield stays empty.
textes.Seul le premier grand sceau de Richard I: Only the first great seal of Richard I shows his arms from before 1198; their tinctures are not known.
textes.Sur le second grand sceau de Richard Iᵉʳ: On the second great seal of Richard I (1198). John took them up: the design would not change again. French heralds call them “leopards”; English heralds say “lions passant guardant”.
textes.Édouard III revendique la couronne de Fr: Edward III claimed the crown of France: the lilies took the place of honour, in the 1st and 4th quarters, acknowledging the precedence of the Kingdom of France.
textes.Richard II accole les armes prêtées à Éd: Richard II impaled the arms credited to Edward the Confessor, as a sign of mystical union; Henry IV abandoned them.
textes.Henri IV réduit le semé à trois lis, à l: Henry IV reduced the semé to three lilies, in imitation of Charles V of France.
textes.Marie Iʳᵉ et son époux Philippe accolent: Mary I and her husband Philip impaled their arms.
textes.Jacques VI d'Écosse devient Jacques Iᵉʳ: James VI of Scotland became James I of England: Scotland entered the shield, and Ireland with its harp. These are the last arms of the Kingdom of England.
textes.Souverains conjoints, ils accolent leurs: Joint sovereigns, they impaled their arms, the husband on the dexter side; William added the escutcheon of his House of Nassau.
textes.Après la mort de Marie, Guillaume III ga: After Mary's death, William III kept his own arms alone.
textes.Les Actes d'Union : l'Angleterre et l'Éc: The Acts of Union: England and Scotland, now united, share the 1st and 4th quarters; France keeps the 2nd.
textes.George Iᵉʳ, électeur de Hanovre, fait en: George I, Elector of Hanover, brought his German lands into the 4th quarter.
textes.Proclamation du 1ᵉʳ janvier 1801 : les l: Proclamation of 1 January 1801: the lilies of France left the shield, which they had occupied since 1340. Ireland, united with Great Britain, took its rank with England and Scotland; Hanover moved to an escutcheon.
textes.Le Hanovre devenu royaume, la couronne r: Hanover having become a kingdom, the crown replaced the electoral bonnet on the escutcheon.
textes.Victoria ne peut régner sur le Hanovre,: Victoria could not reign over Hanover, subject to Salic law: the escutcheon disappeared. The blazon has not changed since; in Scotland, Scotland moves to the 1st and 4th quarters.
textes.Rois d'Angleterre, puis du Royaume-Uni: Kings of England, then of the United Kingdom
textes.Des rois normands sans armoiries aux tro: From Norman kings without arms to the three lions, then four and a half centuries of the lilies of France — until they left in 1801 — before the three-kingdom shield that has not changed since Victoria.
textes.Dates des règnes : « Liste des monarques: Dates of reigns: “Liste des monarques d'Angleterre” (Wikipedia) until 1707, “List of British monarchs” thereafter. Names link to the French Wikipedia article on the sovereign; the kings and queens the list holds on the margins (Matilda, Henry the Young King, Louis of France, Jane Grey) have their own row.
textes.Armoiries : « Royal arms of England », «: Arms: “Royal arms of England”, “Coat of arms of Great Britain” and “Royal coat of arms of the United Kingdom” for the shields; “English claims to the French throne” for the lilies of France; “Royal supporters of England”, “Royal badges of England” and “Dieu et mon droit” for the supporters, badges and mottoes.
textes.Les supports prêtés aux rois d'avant les: The supporters credited to kings before the Tudors were, for the most part, invented in the Tudor period: the timeline shows them only from 1485. For the same reason, the arms attributed to the Norman kings are not shown.
textes.Couronnes, jarretière et rangée des lis: The crowns, garter and row of lilies are drawn by the encyclopedia. Shields, great arms and insignia come from Wikimedia Commons, each with its author and licence checked on its page:
textes.Le brin de genêt — planta genista en lat: The sprig of broom — planta genista in medieval Latin — gave the dynasty its name.
textes.roi d'Angleterre, et « de France » à par: King of England, and “of France” from 1340
textes.Couché, colleté et enchaîné d'or ; il le: Lodged, gorged and chained or; he had it from his mother, Joan of Kent.
textes.« Souverain » : la plus ancienne devise: “Souverain”: the oldest known motto beneath the royal arms.
textes.Il fait de ce cri de guerre la devise ro: He made this war cry the royal motto; it became fixed only in 1714.
textes.Armé et soies d'or ; c'était déjà son in: Armed and bristled or; it was already his badge before the throne.
textes.Devise personnelle, montrée sous les arm: Personal motto, shown beneath the royal arms.
textes.souverains conjoints d'Angleterre et d'É: joint sovereigns of England and Scotland
textes.reine d'Angleterre et d'Écosse, puis de: Queen of England and Scotland, then of Great Britain
textes.la rose et le chardon sur une même tige: the rose and the thistle on one stem
textes.roi de Grande-Bretagne, puis du Royaume-: King of Great Britain, then of the United Kingdom
textes.Il songe à charger les armes de l'écusso: He thought of charging the arms with the escutcheon of Saxony and a mark for Wales; his advisers talked him out of it.
textes.Entre la mort d'Édouard VI et l'avènemen: Between the death of Edward VI and the accession of Mary, Jane Grey was proclaimed queen; the list does not count her among the sovereigns.
No king: the royal arms lapse. The Protectorate (1653-1659) gave itself arms of its own, visible under “great arms”.
textes.Entre la fuite de Jacques II et l'avènem: Between the flight of James II and the joint accession of William III and Mary II.
textes.Évincée par son cousin Étienne, elle lut: Ousted by her cousin Stephen, she fought for her rights and took the title in 1141.
textes.Sacré en 1170, il règne conjointement av: Crowned in 1170, he reigned jointly with his father Henry II and died before him.
textes.Le futur Louis VIII de France ; la liste: The future Louis VIII of France; the list gives him on the margins.
textes.Proclamée quatre jours après la mort d'É: Proclaimed four days after the death of Edward VI, deposed nine days later.
textes.Le second grand sceau de Richard Iᵉʳ por: The second great seal of Richard I bears three lions: the arms of England are fixed.
textes.Édouard III revendique la couronne de Fr: Edward III claimed the crown of France and quartered his arms with the lilies, in the place of honour.
textes.Édouard III fonde l'ordre de la Jarretiè: Edward III founded the Order of the Garter: “Honi soit qui mal y pense”.
textes.De 1360 à 1369, l'écu revient aux seuls: From 1360 to 1369 the shield went back to the lions alone.
textes.Richard II accole à ses armes celles prê: Richard II impaled his arms with those credited to Edward the Confessor.
textes.Henri IV réduit le semé de France à troi: Henry IV reduced the semé of France to three lilies.
textes.Henri V fait du cri de guerre la devise: Henry V made the war cry the royal motto.
textes.Le dragon rouge et le lévrier blanc sout: The red dragon and the white greyhound support the shield.
textes.Marie Iʳᵉ accole les armes de son époux: Mary I impaled the arms of her Spanish husband.
textes.Jacques VI d'Écosse devient roi d'Anglet: James VI of Scotland became King of England: Scotland and Ireland entered the shield, and the unicorn replaced the dragon.
textes.La monarchie abolie, les armes royales t: The monarchy abolished, the royal arms lapsed; the Protectorate would have its own.
textes.Guillaume III charge les armes de l'écus: William III charged the arms with the escutcheon of his house.
textes.Les Actes d'Union : Angleterre et Écosse: The Acts of Union: England and Scotland share the same quarters.
textes.George Iᵉʳ fait entrer le Hanovre au 4ᵉ: George I brought Hanover into the 4th quarter; “Dieu et mon droit” became the fixed motto.
textes.La France devient une république : la pr: France became a republic: the claim to the French throne no longer had an object, but the lilies stayed in the shield.
textes.Proclamation du 1ᵉʳ janvier 1801 : le ro: Proclamation of 1 January 1801: the King no longer called himself King of France, and the lilies disappeared from the arms after more than four and a half centuries; the claim was abandoned the following year.
textes.Le Hanovre devenu royaume, une couronne: Hanover having become a kingdom, a crown replaced the electoral bonnet.
textes.Exclue du trône de Hanovre par la loi sa: Excluded from the throne of Hanover by Salic law, Victoria removed its escutcheon: the arms took their present form.
textes.La partition de l'Irlande ne change rien: The partition of Ireland changed nothing in the arms: the harp stays in the 3rd quarter.
textes.Supports : un dragon rouge et un lévrier: Supporters: a red dragon and a white greyhound gorged gules
textes.Supports : le lion couronné d'Angleterre: Supporters: the crowned lion of England and the chained unicorn of Scotland
textes.Supports : le lion couronné et le dragon: Supporters: the crowned lion and the red dragon, the Stuart unicorn set aside
textes.Les Hanovre, rois de Grande-Bretagne: The Hanoverians, Kings of Great Britain
textes.Le Royaume-Uni, sans les lis: The United Kingdom, without the lilies
textes.Cimier : un lion couronné sur la couronn: Crest: a crowned lion on the imperial crown, on the royal helm
textes.Édouard III se dit roi de France et écar: Edward III called himself King of France and quartered his arms with the lilies, in the place of honour.
textes.Revenus en 1369, les lis restent dans l': Back in 1369, the lilies stayed in the shield of every king, Tudors, Stuarts and Hanoverians included, until the proclamation of 1 January 1801.
textes.La couronne du cimier, jusque-là cercle: The crown of the crest, until then a circlet with fleurons, received crosses pattée under Henry VI.
Edward IV closed it with an arch.
textes.Henri VII lui donne deux arches ; depuis: Henry VII gave it two arches; since the late 17th century, a circlet with alternating crosses pattée and lilies, two arches, orb and cross.
textes.Édouard III fonde l'ordre de la Jarretiè: Edward III founded the Order of the Garter in 1348; its motto, “Honi soit qui mal y pense”, often surrounds the royal shield — since when, the sources read do not say.
textes.Henri VII : un dragon rouge et un lévrie: Henry VII: a red dragon and a white greyhound.
textes.dragon et lévrier, puis lion et dragon: dragon and greyhound, then lion and dragon
textes.Henri VIII garde d'abord ceux de son pèr: Henry VIII at first kept his father's, then took the crowned lion of England and the red dragon.
textes.Édouard VI garde le lion et le dragon de: Edward VI kept his father's lion and dragon.
textes.Marie Iʳᵉ : l'aigle de son époux Philipp: Mary I: the eagle of her husband Philip and the lion of England.
textes.Élisabeth Iʳᵉ reprend ceux de son père ;: Elizabeth I took up her father's; the dragon is sometimes gold.
textes.Jacques Iᵉʳ remplace le dragon par la li: James I replaced the dragon with the unicorn of Scotland.
textes.Le Protectorat garde le lion, reprend le: The Protectorate kept the lion, took the dragon back and set aside the Stuart unicorn.
textes.Le lion et la licorne, inchangés depuis: The lion and the unicorn, unchanged since the Restoration.
textes.Les pages lues ne donnent d'armoiries à: The pages read give arms to no duke before Odo II: it was he, the list says, who first adopted the arms of Burgundy.
textes.Adoptées par Eudes II, ces armes sont ce: Adopted by Odo II, these arms were those of all the Capetian dukes until 1361. Cadets differenced them: the Count of Nevers added a bordure indented gules, the Lord of Montagu a quarter of ermine, the Prince of Morea a quarter of Villehardouin, the son of Odo IV a fleur-de-lis or on the quarter.
textes.Philippe le Hardi, quatrième fils de Jea: Philip the Bold, fourth son of John II, bore the arms of France differenced with a bordure compony argent and gules, which he quartered with the old arms of Burgundy on becoming duke in 1364.
textes.Jean sans Peur, fils de Marguerite de Fl: John the Fearless, son of Margaret of Flanders, set the lion of Flanders at the centre.
textes.Après l'annexion du Brabant et du Limbou: After annexing Brabant and Limburg, Philip the Good brought them into the shield. Charles the Bold did not change it.
textes.Au mariage de Marie avec l'archiduc Maxi: On the marriage of Mary to Archduke Maximilian (1477), the husband's arms and the duchess's shared the shield.
textes.Fils de Marie et de Maximilien, Philippe: Son of Mary and Maximilian, Philip kept the arms of Burgundy and joined those of Austria to them. Later King of Castile, he would also quarter them with the arms of the Catholic Monarchs. The file shows his arms as duke in 1483-1485.
textes.Quatre siècles et demi d'un même bandé d: Four and a half centuries of the same bendy or and azure with a bordure gules, differenced at every turn — label, bordure indented, quarter — then the fleur-de-lis of the Valois, the lion of Flanders, Brabant and Limburg, until the death of Charles at Nancy.
textes.Dates des règnes : « Liste des ducs de B: Dates of reigns: “Liste des ducs de Bourgogne” (Wikipedia), from Robert I (1032), founder of the first Capetian house of Burgundy. Earlier dukes (Bosonids, Robertians, Ivrea) are left out, as are the Kings of France who briefly held the title (Robert the Pious, Henry I). The timeline stops at Philip the Handsome (1506): after him, the Habsburgs of Burgundy, then the Kings of Spain, are dukes in title only (see the Habsburg and Spain timelines). Names link to the French Wikipedia article on the duke.
textes.Armoiries : « Armorial des Capétiens » (: Arms: “Armorial des Capétiens” (Wikipedia), which blazons the arms of the Dukes of Burgundy and those of their children and brothers, and, for Philip the Handsome, “Coat of arms of Spain” (English Wikipedia). The arms of the cadets, Counts of Nevers and Lords of Montagu, are differences: the chapter in the encyclopedia explains them.
textes.Le règne de Jean II le Bon (1361-1363 se: The reign of John II the Good (1361-1363 according to the list) is shown separately as a reunion with the crown: he did not merge the duchy into the royal domain, and gave it to his son in 1364.
textes.Les couronnes ne sont pas dessinées. Écu: The crowns are not drawn. Shields and great arms come from Wikimedia Commons, each with its author and licence checked on its page:
textes.Fils du roi Robert II le Pieux et de Con: Son of King Robert II the Pious and Constance of Arles: he founded the first Capetian house of Burgundy.
textes.Il adopte le premier les armes de Bourgo: He was the first to adopt the arms of Burgundy.
textes.Régence d'Alix de Vergy, sa mère, de 121: Regency of Alix of Vergy, his mother, from 1218 to 1228. Titular King of Thessalonica from 1266 to 1272.
textes.Troisième fils d'Hugues IV ; père de Mar: Third son of Hugh IV; father of Margaret of Burgundy (married to Louis X) and of Joan (married to Philip VI).
textes.Cadet, il brise d'abord les armes d'une: A cadet, he at first differenced the arms with a bordure indented before the death of his elder brother. Grandson of Saint Louis through his mother.
textes.Né posthume à Rouvres-en-Plaine en 1346,: Born posthumously at Rouvres-en-Plaine in 1346, he succeeded his grandfather; regency of Joan of Auvergne, his mother, from 1349 to 1361. He died of plague at fifteen: he was the last Capetian duke.
textes.Philippe, quatrième fils de Jean II, por: Philip, fourth son of John II, bore the arms of France differenced with a bordure compony before becoming duke.
textes.Quatrième et dernier fils du roi Jean II: Fourth and last son of King John II the Good. John II passed the duchy to him three years after claiming it: this is the second house of Burgundy.
textes.Duc de Bourgogne, de Lothier et de Braba: Duke of Burgundy, Lothier and Brabant, Count of Flanders, Hainault and Holland.
textes.Jimmy44, d'après un fichier d'Ipankonin: Jimmy44, after a file by Ipankonin
textes.Charles, fils aîné du duc, brise les arm: Charles, the Duke's eldest son, differenced his father's arms with a label argent; on becoming duke in 1467, he removed the label.
textes.Fils unique de Philippe le Bon, dernier: Only son of Philip the Good, last man of the House of Valois-Burgundy; he died at Nancy, leaving only a daughter.
textes.Cinquième et dernière duchesse de la bra: Fifth and last duchess of the Valois-Burgundy branch. She married Archduke Maximilian of Habsburg, who took over the titles and possessions of the Valois-Burgundy, the Burgundian Netherlands, the County of Burgundy, the Golden Fleece and the arms.
textes.Premier des ducs « Habsbourg » de la lis: First of the “Habsburg” dukes in the list (1482-1506), son of Mary of Burgundy and Maximilian; his son Charles V succeeded him as duke in 1506.
textes.À la mort de Philippe de Rouvres, Jean I: On the death of Philip of Rouvres, John II, second Valois king, claimed the duchy on 28 December 1361. He did not merge it into the royal domain: the duchy remained a separate feudal entity, defended by the Burgundian estates. Henry of Bar was its first governor (1362); in 1364 the King passed it to his son Philip the Bold. The list gives him a reign from 1361 to 1363.
textes.Robert, fils du roi Robert II le Pieux,: Robert, son of King Robert II the Pious, became Duke of Burgundy.
textes.Eudes II adopte le premier les armes : b: Odo II was the first to adopt the arms: bendy of six or and azure, a bordure gules. They would remain those of the dukes until 1361.
textes.Les cadets brisent les armes ducales : b: Cadets differenced the ducal arms: a bordure indented for the Count of Nevers, taken up by Odo IV while his elder brother Hugh V was still alive, a quarter of ermine for Montagu, of Villehardouin for Morea, a fleur-de-lis on the quarter for a son of Odo IV.
textes.Philippe de Rouvres meurt de la peste à: Philip of Rouvres died of plague at fifteen. John II the Good claimed the duchy, which he gave in 1364 to his son Philip the Bold.
textes.Philippe le Hardi écartèle ses armes de: Philip the Bold quartered his arms as a son of France (the bordure compony argent and gules) with the old arms of Burgundy.
textes.Philippe le Bon fait entrer dans l'écu l: Philip the Good brought annexed Brabant and Limburg into the shield.
textes.Charles, comte de Charolais, portait les: Charles, Count of Charolais, bore his father's arms differenced with a label argent; on becoming duke, he removed it.
textes.Charles meurt à Nancy. Le duché de Bourg: Charles died at Nancy. The Duchy of Burgundy was annexed to the Kingdom of France; the County of Burgundy (Franche-Comté) and the Netherlands passed to the Habsburgs through the marriage of Mary to Maximilian.
textes.Philippe le Beau, fils de Marie et de Ma: Philip the Handsome, son of Mary and Maximilian, inherited the titles, the arms and the Golden Fleece. The Habsburg Dukes of Burgundy succeed one another until 1918, a courtesy title from 1795 for the Austrian Habsburgs.
textes.La nature de l'inféodation de 1364 est d: The nature of the 1364 enfeoffment is debated: the King of France and the Habsburgs dispute the title.
textes.Philippe le Bon : l'écu dans son décor: Philip the Good: the shield in its setting
textes.Collier de la Toison d'or (d'après le de: Collar of the Golden Fleece (from the drawing in the file)
textes.Deux bâtons noueux passés en sautoir der: Two ragged staves in saltire behind the shield: the cross of Burgundy (from the drawing)
textes.Le fichier montre l'écu de Philippe III: The file shows the shield of Philip III the Good with its ornaments; the article on the dukes does not describe these ornaments.
textes.Charles le Téméraire : l'écu et ses supp: Charles the Bold: the shield and its supporters
textes.Supports : deux lions (d'après le dessin: Supporters: two lions (from the drawing in the file)
textes.Le fichier est dessiné d'après un tablea: The file is drawn after an armorial panel of Charles the Bold; the label of the Count of Charolais is no longer there.
textes.Les sources lues ne prêtent d'armoiries: The sources read credit arms to no king before William the Lion: the shield stays empty.
textes.Le lion et le double trescheur: The lion and the double tressure
textes.Un lion rampant se distingue nettement s: A rampant lion is clearly visible on the seal of Alexander II; its adoption is credited to his father William the Lion, whose seal shows no trace of it. The shield then passes from king to king almost unchanged. The tressure of lilies, said to come from the Auld Alliance with France, is attested before 1295, when that alliance begins: the explanation is unlikely. Under James III, Parliament once decided to remove the tressure; it was soon restored, at first without its upper edge, then whole.
textes.Au mariage de Marie avec le dauphin, en: On Mary's marriage to the Dauphin in 1558, the arms of Scotland were impaled with those of Francis, whose own shield as Dauphin brought them in as a quarter to mark his title of king consort.
textes.François devient roi de France en 1559 :: Francis became King of France in 1559: Mary's arms followed her rank as queen consort.
textes.Veuve de François en 1560, Marie garde l: Widowed of Francis in 1560, Mary kept the impalement until her remarriage to Darnley in 1565, then went back to the lion alone.
textes.Jacques VI hérite d'Angleterre et d'Irla: James VI inherited England and Ireland in 1603: the arms of England, already quartered with France, joined the lion of Scotland, and the harp of Ireland entered the shield. In the version used in Scotland, the lion keeps the places of honour (1 and 4).
textes.Les armes de 1603 reviennent avec Charle: The arms of 1603 return with Charles II; they were not used during the Commonwealth.
textes.Marie II et Guillaume II règnent ensembl: Mary II and William II reigned together and impaled their arms, identical except that William bore the escutcheon of the House of Nassau.
textes.À la mort de Marie, Guillaume porte seul: On Mary's death, William bore his arms alone.
textes.Un seul écu — le lion de gueules dans so: A single shield — the red lion within its double tressure — crosses five centuries of Scottish kings almost unchanged. It blurs only with Mary Stuart, impaled with the arms of France, and then fades in 1603 into the quartering that unites the three crowns.
textes.Dates des règnes : « Liste des monarques: Dates of reigns: “Liste des monarques d'Écosse” (Wikipedia). The timeline begins with Duncan I (1034): the kings of the House of Alpin (843-1034) have, in the sources read, no arms, and arms did not exist before the 12th century. Names link to the French Wikipedia article on the sovereign; Edward Balliol, whom the list counts among the kings but who usurped the throne of David II, has his row “On the margins”.
textes.Armoiries : « Coat of arms of Scotland »: Arms: “Coat of arms of Scotland” (English Wikipedia) for the history of the arms, supporters and variants; the shields come from Commons. The exact dates of each version are those the page gives; when it gives only a year, the timeline is no more precise.
textes.Les rois sont presque tous au lion : la: Nearly all the kings bear the lion: the list says nothing of the arms of Margaret the Maid of Norway, or of those of John Balliol, and the timeline leaves them the lion of the crown. At the end, the Union of 1707 closes the line: the arms of Great Britain in Scotland (1707-1714) are not included.
textes.Marguerite Iʳᵉ, la Vierge de Norvège: Margaret I, the Maid of Norway
textes.Reconnue reine par les Gardiens de l'Éco: Recognised as queen by the Guardians of Scotland, she died in Orkney before reaching her kingdom. The list says nothing of her arms; the timeline leaves her those of the crown.
textes.Jean Stewart, futur Robert III, porte le: John Stewart, the future Robert III, bore the royal lion differenced with a label while he was only heir to the throne.
Prisoner in England from 1406 to 1424. He introduced the two lions as supporters on his privy seal.
textes.Son sceau privé porte deux licornes, au: His privy seal bears two unicorns, instead of the usual two lions.
textes.Reine de France de 1559 à 1560 par son m: Queen of France from 1559 to 1560 by her marriage to Francis II; forced to abdicate in favour of her son in 1567.
textes.roi des Écossais, et d'Angleterre à part: King of Scots, and of England from 1603
textes.roi des Écossais, d'Angleterre et d'Irla: King of Scots, of England and of Ireland
textes.Proclamé par le Parlement d'Écosse le 5: Proclaimed by the Parliament of Scotland on 5 February 1649, crowned at Scone on 1 January 1651, defeated by Cromwell at Worcester on 3 September 1651.
textes.Fuit la Grande-Bretagne en décembre 1688: Fled Great Britain in December 1688; on 11 April 1689 the Parliament of Scotland declared him an unconstitutional monarch because of his Catholic religion.
textes.reine des Écossais, d'Angleterre et d'Ir: Queen of Scots, of England and of Ireland
textes.Anne reprend la version de 1603 jusqu'à: Anne took up the 1603 version until the Union: on 1 May 1707 she became the first Queen of Great Britain.
textes.La mort de Marguerite ouvre une crise de: Margaret's death opened a succession crisis lasting nearly two years, until the coronation of John Balliol.
textes.Jean Balliol abdique à Stracathro après: John Balliol abdicated at Stracathro after the defeat at Dunbar; the throne remained without a crowned king until Robert I Bruce.
textes.Après Worcester, l'Écosse est placée sou: After Worcester, Scotland was placed under military government, then joined to the Commonwealth of England by the Tender of Union of 1652, which dissolved the Scottish Parliament. Cromwell governed it from 1653 to 1658, then his son Richard until 1659.
textes.Entre la fuite de Jacques VII et la proc: Between the flight of James VII and the proclamation of William and Mary by the Parliament of Scotland.
textes.Sacré à Scone, il usurpe le trône de Dav: Crowned at Scone, he usurped the throne of David II from 1332 to 1341, then abdicated in 1356 at Wheatley Hill.
textes.On lui attribue l'adoption du lion rampa: The adoption of the rampant lion is credited to him, but his seal shows no trace of it.
textes.Le lion ne se lit nettement que sur le s: The lion can be read clearly only on the seal of his son Alexander II (1214).
textes.Le revers du grand sceau d'Alexandre II: The reverse of the great seal of Alexander II shows a rampant lion, on the shield as on the horse's saddle.
textes.Marguerite, reconnue reine par les Gardi: Margaret, recognised as queen by the Guardians of Scotland, died in Orkney before reaching her kingdom: the throne stayed disputed for nearly two years.
textes.Robert Iᵉʳ est sacré à Scone le 27 mars: Robert I was crowned at Scone on 27 March 1306, after ten years without a crowned king.
textes.Robert II, fils de Marjorie Bruce, ouvre: Robert II, son of Marjorie Bruce, opened the reign of the House of Stewart; Mary Stuart would later frenchify the name to Stuart.
textes.Jacques Iᵉʳ introduit deux lions comme s: James I introduced two lions as supporters on his privy seal, and a single unicorn elsewhere. The lions would remain almost without a break until 1603.
textes.Marie épouse le dauphin François : ses a: Mary married the Dauphin Francis: her arms were impaled with his, then with those of France when he came to the throne (1559). She gave this up in 1565 and returned to the lion alone.
textes.Jacques VI hérite d'Angleterre et d'Irla: James VI inherited England and Ireland: the lion of Scotland was quartered with the arms of England (already charged with France) and the harp of Ireland.
textes.Charles II fait inscrire au registre pub: Charles II had the shield, helm, unicorns and motto of the King of Scots entered in the Public Register of arms of Scotland.
textes.Guillaume II et Marie II accolent leurs: William II and Mary II impaled their arms; William's bear the escutcheon of the House of Nassau at the centre.
textes.L'Écosse et l'Angleterre fusionnent dans: Scotland and England merged into the Kingdom of Great Britain: the title of King of Scots disappeared.
textes.Jacques VI : l'écu des trois couronnes: James VI: the shield of the three crowns
textes.Supports : une licorne et un lion, porta: Supporters: a unicorn and a lion, bearing the banners of Saint Andrew and Saint George (from the drawing in the file)
textes.Cimier : un lion assis de face, couronné: Crest: a lion sejant affronté, crowned, holding a sword and a sceptre
textes.Le fichier est daté de 1603 à 1649 ; la: The file is dated 1603 to 1649; the same version served Charles II until 1651.
textes.Guillaume et Marie : les armes accolées: William and Mary: the arms impaled
textes.Devise de l'ordre du Chardon : Nemo me i: Motto of the Order of the Thistle: Nemo me impune lacessit, on a blue scroll
textes.La devise de l'ordre du Chardon paraît s: The motto of the Order of the Thistle appears on a blue scroll beneath the shield after the reign of Charles II; until then, only the collar of the Order featured on the arms.
textes.Devise de l'ordre du Chardon : Nemo me i: Motto of the Order of the Thistle: Nemo me impune lacessit
textes.Faute de fichier propre au règne d'Anne,: For lack of a file specific to the reign of Anne, the 1603 version the source says was hers is used.
textes.Jacques Iᵉʳ introduit deux lions comme s: James I introduced two lions as supporters on his privy seal, and a single unicorn elsewhere.
textes.Jacques V fait exception : son sceau pri: James V is the exception: his privy seal bears two unicorns.
textes.Marie revient aux lions sur son sceau pr: Mary went back to lions on her privy seal, but used two unicorns on her great seal: the first to do so.
textes.Les lions servent presque sans interrupt: The lions served almost without a break until the Union of the Crowns.
textes.Jacques VI prend une licorne et un lion: James VI took a unicorn and a lion: the usage that still lasts.
textes.La licorne et le lion reviennent avec Ch: The unicorn and the lion returned with Charles II and remained until the Union.
textes.Les sources lues ne prêtent d'armoiries: The sources read credit arms to no King of Aragon before Alfonso II; the oldest evidence of the pallets is a seal of 1150 of Ramon Berenguer IV, Count of Barcelona and Prince of Aragon.
textes.Armes parlantes : le château (castellum): Canting arms: the castle (castellum) says Castile, the lion says León. The Kings of León first bore a lion purpure, then gules; it was Ferdinand III, King of Castile and León, who united the two shields and produced the first quartering.
textes.Même composition ; le lion se blasonne d: Same composition; the lion is blazoned purpure or gules depending on the author.
textes.Le fichier ne date pas son dessin plus p: The file dates its drawing no more precisely than by the century.
textes.L'un des plus anciens écus d'Europe. Sa: One of the oldest shields in Europe. Its first trace is a seal of Ramon Berenguer IV (1150) for Catalan authors; Aragonese authors see undeniable evidence only from Alfonso II. The old armorials attribute it to the Counts of Barcelona, who acquired Aragon by marriage.
textes.Les armes d'Isabelle et de Ferdinand, do: The arms of Isabella and Ferdinand, whose marriage united Spain. The file is titled “Isabella of Castile”.
textes.La conquête de Grenade se marque par l'a: The conquest of Granada is marked by adding a quarter of Granada enté en point: argent, a pomegranate proper, stalked and leaved with two leaves vert.
textes.À la mort d'Isabelle (1504), Ferdinand a: On Isabella's death (1504), Ferdinand gave up the joint arms for a shield tierced in pale: Castile-León, Aragon-Naples-Sicily, Aragon. The annexation of Navarre (1513) brought the last change.
textes.À la mort d'Isabelle, son gendre, l'arch: On Isabella's death, her son-in-law, Archduke Philip, quartered his own arms with those of the Catholic Monarchs. As his highest title was only archducal, the Spanish quarters took precedence over his.
textes.Les armes abrégées de Jeanne et de Charl: The abridged arms of Joanna and Charles I, from 1504 to about 1555.
textes.Après son élection impériale (1519), Cha: After his imperial election (1519), Charles set his arms on the breast of an eagle; from 1530 some versions place the Spanish quarters in 1 and 4 and the Austrian quarters in 2 and 3.
textes.Philippe II, roi consort d'Angleterre: Philip II, king consort of England
textes.Armes de Philippe II comme monarque espa: Arms of Philip II as Spanish monarch and husband of Mary I of England, from 1556 to 1558.
textes.Philippe II reprend d'abord les armes si: Philip II at first took up his father's simplified arms: per fess, the Spanish quarters in chief and the Austrian in base.
textes.À l'union avec le Portugal (1580), un éc: At the union with Portugal (1580), an escutcheon of Portugal came to the honour point; the shield, under a royal crown with three visible arches, is surrounded by the collar of the Golden Fleece. Lost in 1640, Portugal stayed in the shield as arms of pretension until 1668.
textes.Charles II renonce à l'écusson de Portug: Charles II gave up the escutcheon of Portugal in 1668.
textes.Philippe V, petit-fils de Louis XIV, fai: Philip V, grandson of Louis XIV, had his arms drawn in November 1700 by the French herald Clairambault. The abridged arms are quarterly Castile and León, enté en point Granada, with the escutcheon of Anjou overall. The collars of the Golden Fleece and the Holy Spirit surround the shield.
textes.Charles III, fils d'Élisabeth Farnèse, m: Charles III, son of Elisabeth Farnese, changed the arms in 1761, with the collars of the Golden Fleece and the Order of Charles III. The abridged arms, with the Pillars of Hercules and the motto PLUS ULTRA, became the overall escutcheon of the arms of State. The escutcheon of Anjou appears more and more often without a bordure, then as an escutcheon of France.
textes.Joseph proclame ses armes en 1808. Il n': Joseph proclaimed his arms in 1808. He was recognised neither by the people nor by the Cortes; the Spanish saw him as an intruder king.
textes.Le gouvernement provisoire de 1868 avait: The provisional government of 1868 had adopted the present territorial arms, under a mural crown; Amadeo restored the royal crown and set an escutcheon of Savoy at the fess point. Few Spanish arms bear the escutcheon of Aosta.
textes.Le décret du 8 janvier 1875 rétablit les: The decree of 8 January 1875 restored the arms from before 29 September 1868. In practice the escutcheon of Anjou appears without its bordure, a sign of descent from the Bourbons of France. The King continued to bear the great arms of Charles III personally; Alfonso XIII merged the two series in 1924.
textes.En 1938, Franco rétablit des éléments de: In 1938 Franco restored elements of the House of Trastámara: the eagle of Saint John, the yoke and the sheaf of arrows.
textes.Un écu intermédiaire, de 1977 à 1981, av: An interim shield, from 1977 to 1981, before the law fixing the present arms.
textes.Fixées par la loi 33/1981 du 5 octobre :: Fixed by Law 33/1981 of 5 October: the Pillars of Hercules bear the motto PLUS ULTRA, “further beyond”, and the royal crown is closed with four arches. Some heralds criticise the drawing as too close to a logotype.
textes.Un château et un lion : deux royaumes, d: A castle and a lion: two kingdoms, whose canting arms Ferdinand III brought together in 1230 in the first quartering, which would serve for two and a half centuries, until the marriage of Isabella and Ferdinand of Aragon.
textes.Trois frises se suivent : Castille et Le: Three timelines follow one another: Castile and León (1230-1474), Aragon (1035-1479) and Spain (since 1474), which takes up the two crowns from the marriage of Isabella and Ferdinand. The exact dates of reigns come from three Wikipedia lists: “Liste des souverains de Castille” (section “Couronne de Castille”), “Liste des souverains d'Aragon” and “Liste des rois et reines d'Espagne”; for Isabella II, the article devoted to her. Names link to the French Wikipedia article on the sovereign.
textes.Armoiries : « Coat of arms of Spain » et: Arms: “Coat of arms of Spain” and “Coat of arms of the Crown of Aragon” (English Wikipedia). The sources read credit arms to no King of Aragon before Alfonso II; Catalan authors date the pallets to a seal of 1150, Aragonese authors to the reign of Alfonso II, and the timeline follows the latter for the kings, and says so. The Counts of Castile, the Kings of Asturias and León before 1230 and the Counts of Aragon are left out.
textes.Les règnes qui se chevauchent (Jeanne et: Overlapping reigns (Joanna and Philip, Joanna and Charles) are shown one after the other; the three rival kings of John II of Aragon (1462-1472) are in the row “On the margins”. Periods without a king (1868-1870, 1873-1874, 1931-1975) are marked with a stroke. The Spanish Habsburgs also appear in the Habsburg timeline, which is concerned with the house rather than the kingdom.
textes.Les couronnes ne sont pas dessinées. Les: The crowns are not drawn. The shields and great arms of the three timelines come from Wikimedia Commons, each with its author and licence checked on its page:
textes.Roi de Castille, il hérite de León en 12: King of Castile, he inherited León in 1230 and united the two kingdoms, with a shield uniting their arms.
textes.Régence de Marie de Molina de 1295 à 130: Regency of Maria de Molina from 1295 to 1301.
textes.Surnommé « le Cruel » par ses détracteur: Nicknamed “the Cruel” by his detractors, he faced the rebellions of his half-brother Henry; defeated and captured at Montiel (1369), he was murdered at a meeting with him.
textes.Fils illégitime d'Alphonse XI, comte de: Illegitimate son of Alfonso XI, Count of Trastámara: he founded the House of Trastámara, a cadet branch of the House of Ivrea.
textes.Régence de Ferdinand Iᵉʳ d'Aragon de 140: Regency of Ferdinand I of Aragon from 1406 to 1410.
textes.Ferdinand III, déjà roi de Castille, hér: Ferdinand III, already King of Castile, inherited León: he combined the arms of the two kingdoms.
textes.Henri II, fils illégitime d'Alphonse XI,: Henry II, illegitimate son of Alfonso XI, founded the House of Trastámara, a cadet branch of Ivrea, without changing the shield.
textes.Jean II et Henri IV : l'écu aux lions: John II and Henry IV: the shield with lions
textes.Supports : deux lions d'or (d'après le d: Supporters: two golden lions (from the drawing in the file)
textes.Quatre pals de gueules sur or : l'un des: Four pallets gules on or: one of the oldest shields in Europe, born of the Counts of Barcelona and borne by the Kings of Aragon from Alfonso II, until Ferdinand combined it, in 1479, with that of Castile.
textes.Premier roi d'Aragon après sa victoire d: First King of Aragon after his victory at Tafalla over his half-brother García.
textes.Aussi roi de Navarre, sous le nom de San: Also King of Navarre, as Sancho V.
textes.En 1137, sans abdiquer, il délègue son a: In 1137, without abdicating, he delegated his authority to his son-in-law Ramon Berenguer IV, Prince of Aragon and Count of Barcelona: it is from the latter that the oldest seal with the pallets comes (1150).
textes.Fille de Ramire II. Son mariage avec Ray: Daughter of Ramiro II. Her marriage to Ramon Berenguer IV united Aragon and the County of Barcelona (1137).
textes.Premier roi d'Aragon et comte de Barcelo: First King of Aragon and Count of Barcelona: he bore both titles, which his successors would keep. For Aragonese authors, the pallets are undeniable only from his reign.
textes.Vainqueur aux Navas de Tolosa en 1212, i: Victor at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212, he died at Muret in 1213.
textes.Conquérant de Valence, de Majorque et d': Conqueror of Valencia, Majorca and Ibiza; author of the Llibre dels feyts.
textes.Il fait dessiner une version de l'écu de: He had a version of the kings' shield drawn, with the banner with a blue and white cross that he attributed to the old Kings of Aragon, and the pallets to the Counts of Barcelona.
textes.Mort sans descendance : dernier souverai: Died without issue: last sovereign of the House of Barcelona.
textes.Petit-fils de Pierre IV par sa mère, dés: Grandson of Peter IV through his mother, chosen by the Compromise of Caspe.
textes.De 1462 à 1472, la Catalogne et l'Aragon: From 1462 to 1472, Catalonia and Aragon rose up and recognised rival kings, all descendants of Peter IV.
textes.Martin Iᵉʳ meurt sans descendance ; Ferd: Martin I died without issue; Ferdinand, chosen by the Compromise of Caspe, succeeded him in 1412.
textes.Également roi de Castille et de León sou: Also King of Castile and León as Henry IV.
textes.Infant et connétable de Portugal, il pre: Infante and Constable of Portugal, he took the title King of the Catalans.
textes.Également roi de Naples, duc d'Anjou et: Also King of Naples, Duke of Anjou and Count of Provence.
textes.Le sceau de Raymond-Bérenger IV: The seal of Ramon Berenguer IV
textes.Le plus ancien témoignage des pals, pour: The oldest evidence of the pallets, for Catalan authors: a seal of the Count of Barcelona and Prince of Aragon.
textes.Les auteurs aragonais contestent ce scea: Aragonese authors dispute this seal: for them, the first undeniable evidence dates from the reign of Alfonso II.
textes.Alphonse II, fils de Pétronille et de Ra: Alfonso II, son of Petronilla and Ramon Berenguer IV, was both King of Aragon and Count of Barcelona, two titles all his successors would bear.
textes.Pierre IV fait dessiner une version de l: Peter IV had a version of the kings' shield drawn, in which the pallets go to the Counts of Barcelona and the blue and white cross to the old Kings of Aragon.
textes.Le compromis de Caspe désigne Ferdinand,: The Compromise of Caspe chose Ferdinand, grandson of Peter IV through his mother, after the death of Martin I without issue.
textes.Pierre IV et les rois d'Aragon : l'écu a: Peter IV and the Kings of Aragon: the shield with its crest
textes.Une bannière à croix bleue et blanche, q: A banner with a blue and white cross, which Peter IV attributed to the old Kings of Aragon
textes.Le fichier donne cette version comme cel: The file gives this version as that of the 13th-15th centuries; according to the article, it is due to Peter IV.
textes.Des Rois catholiques à Felipe VI : l'écu: From the Catholic Monarchs to Felipe VI: the shield of Spain takes in the kingdoms (Aragon, Granada, Navarre), Portugal (1580-1668), then the escutcheon of Anjou, before returning in 1981 to the four quarters and the pomegranate.
textes.reine de Castille ; Ferdinand, roi d'Ara: Queen of Castile; Ferdinand, King of Aragon from 1479
textes.Isabelle est reine de Castille et León d: Isabella was Queen of Castile and León from 1474 to 1504, and, by marriage, Queen of Aragon (1479-1504); Ferdinand, king consort of Castile, was King of Aragon from 1479 to 1516. The two crowns remained legally separate. The title “Catholic Monarchs” was granted to them in 1496.
textes.Fils de Maximilien Iᵉʳ et de Marie de Bo: Son of Maximilian I and Mary of Burgundy, founder of the Spanish Habsburg dynasty; husband of Joanna the Mad.
textes.Jeanne Iʳᵉ la Folle et Ferdinand II: Joanna I the Mad and Ferdinand II
textes.reine de Castille ; Ferdinand, roi d'Ara: Queen of Castile; Ferdinand, King of Aragon
textes.Reine de Castille de 1504 à 1555, reine: Queen of Castile from 1504 to 1555, Queen of Aragon from 1516, Joanna “never in fact really reigned”. Ferdinand remained King of Aragon until his death on 25 January 1516, when all the Spains were united under one sceptre.
textes.roi d'Aragon et co-roi de Castille avec: King of Aragon and co-king of Castile with his mother, then king of both
textes.Roi d'Aragon par le testament de Ferdina: King of Aragon by Ferdinand's will, then co-king of Castile with his mother Joanna; sole king of both crowns from 12 April 1555 to 16 January 1556, when he abdicated in favour of Philip. Emperor since 1519, he set his arms on an imperial eagle.
textes.Aussi roi d'Angleterre de 1554 à 1558 pa: Also King of England from 1554 to 1558 by his marriage to Mary Tudor, and King of Portugal from 1580 as Philip I. With him, the arms of the monarchy became fixed for the rest of the House of Austria.
textes.Aussi roi de Portugal sous le nom de Phi: Also King of Portugal as Philip II.
textes.Aussi roi de Portugal (Philippe III) jus: Also King of Portugal (Philip III) until 1640; he nevertheless kept the escutcheon of Portugal as arms of pretension until 1668.
textes.Régence de Marie-Anne d'Autriche de 1665: Regency of Mariana of Austria from 1665 to 1675. His death without issue led to the War of the Spanish Succession.
textes.Petit-fils de Louis XIV, choisi pour hér: Grandson of Louis XIV, chosen as heir by Charles II, he abdicated in favour of his eldest son Louis.
textes.Mort de la variole après huit mois de rè: Died of smallpox after eight months' reign, much loved by the Spanish people.
textes.Il remonte sur le trône à la mort de son: He returned to the throne on his son's death and held it until his own.
textes.Fils de Philippe V et d'Élisabeth Farnès: Son of Philip V and Elisabeth Farnese, he was Duke of Parma then King of Naples and Sicily. He changed the arms in 1761.
textes.Contraint d'abdiquer le 19 mars 1808 en: Forced to abdicate on 19 March 1808 in favour of his son Ferdinand after the Aranjuez uprising, then on 5 May in favour of Napoleon.
textes.Contraint d'abdiquer le 6 mai 1808 en fa: Forced to abdicate on 6 May 1808 in favour of Napoleon.
textes.Frère de Napoléon, auparavant roi de Nap: Brother of Napoleon, previously King of Naples. Seen by most Spaniards as an intruder king, he abdicated after the Battle of Vitoria.
textes.Rétabli par le traité de Valençay. Il ré: Restored by the Treaty of Valençay. He restored the arms of Charles III, great and abridged.
textes.Régences de Marie-Christine (1833-1840): Regencies of Maria Christina (1833-1840) then of Espartero (1840-1843). She went into exile after the revolution of 1868 and abdicated in 1870 in favour of her son Alfonso.
textes.Fils cadet de Victor-Emmanuel II, élu ro: Younger son of Victor Emmanuel II, elected king by the Cortes on 16 November 1870; he abdicated on 11 February 1873.
textes.Fils posthume d'Alphonse XII ; régence d: Posthumous son of Alfonso XII; regency of Maria Christina of Austria until 1902. He went into exile on the proclamation of the Second Republic, on 14 April 1931. In 1924 he had merged the arms of State and his personal arms into a single shield.
textes.Choisi par Franco au détriment de son pè: Chosen by Franco over his father, he became king on the dictator's death and was crowned on 27 November 1975. He abdicated on 18 June 2014.
textes.Roi depuis le lendemain de l'abdication: King since the day after his father's abdication.
textes.Après la révolution de 1868, le gouverne: After the revolution of 1868, the provisional government adopted the present territorial arms, under a mural crown. Amadeo was elected king by the Cortes on 16 November 1870.
textes.Proclamée le 11 février 1873, au lendema: Proclaimed on 11 February 1873, the day after Amadeo's abdication; it lasted twenty-three months and saw five presidents.
textes.Alphonse XIII naît après la mort de son: Alfonso XIII was born after his father's death: the list gives him a reign only from 1886.
textes.La République (1931-1939) reprend les ar: The Republic (1931-1939) took up the territorial arms, with an uncrowned lion in the second quarter; then Franco's State, which in 1938 restored the eagle of Saint John, the yoke and the sheaf of arrows. This is Spain's longest interregnum: from 1949 Franco decreed the country to be under his regency, pending the Restoration.
textes.Isabelle de Castille et Ferdinand d'Arag: Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon united their crowns: quarterly Castile-León and Aragon, on the breast of an eagle of Saint John under an open royal crown.
textes.La conquête de Grenade se marque par un: The conquest of Granada is marked by a quarter of Granada enté en point, the pomegranate proper.
textes.Philippe le Beau écartèle ses armes avec: Philip the Handsome quartered his arms with those of the Catholic Monarchs, and Ferdinand adopted a tierced shield: Castile-León, Aragon-Naples-Sicily, Aragon.
textes.L'annexion de la Navarre apporte le dern: The annexation of Navarre brought the last change to the arms of Ferdinand the Catholic.
textes.Charles Quint, empereur depuis 1519, pos: Charles V, Emperor since 1519, set his arms on a double-headed eagle, between the Pillars of Hercules and the motto PLUS ULTRA; some versions place the Spanish quarters in 1 and 4.
textes.Avec lui, les armes de la monarchie se f: With him, the arms of the monarchy became fixed for the rest of the House of Austria: per fess, the Spanish quarters in chief and the Austrian in base.
textes.À l'union avec le Portugal, un écusson d: At the union with Portugal, an escutcheon of Portugal came to the honour point of the shield. Lost in 1640, it stayed as arms of pretension until 1668.
textes.Philippe V, petit-fils de Louis XIV, fai: Philip V, grandson of Louis XIV, had his arms drawn by Clairambault: the abridged arms bear the escutcheon of Anjou overall.
textes.Il fait écarteler de six les armes : Ara: He had the arms quartered of six: Aragon, Austria, Farnese, Medici, Burgundy, Brabant, with the Castilian-Leonese escutcheon overall. These arms would last, with interruptions, until 1931.
textes.Joseph Bonaparte proclame de nouvelles a: Joseph Bonaparte proclaimed new arms: six quarters (Castile, León, Aragon, Navarre, Granada, the Indies), the eagle of France overall.
textes.Le gouvernement provisoire adopte l'écu: The provisional government adopted the present shield: Castile, León, Aragon and Navarre, Granada in base, under a mural crown.
textes.Un décret du 8 janvier 1875 rétablit les: A decree of 8 January 1875 restored the arms from before September 1868. The escutcheon of Anjou appears without its bordure; with the death of the Count of Chambord (1883), Alfonso XII bore the arms of France undifferenced.
textes.Franco rétablit des éléments de la maiso: Franco restored elements of the House of Trastámara: the eagle of Saint John, the yoke and the sheaf of arrows.
textes.La loi 33/1981 du 5 octobre fixe les arm: Law 33/1981 of 5 October fixed the present arms, with the oval escutcheon of Anjou overall.
textes.L'écu est entouré du collier de la Toiso: The shield is surrounded by the collar of the Golden Fleece; under Philip V (1700-1761) that of the Holy Spirit is added, under Charles III that of the Order of Charles III.
textes.Les armes des Rois catholiques reposent: The arms of the Catholic Monarchs rest on the breast of an eagle of Saint John, sable, under an open royal crown.
textes.Après 1530, les armes de Charles Quint r: After 1530, the arms of Charles V rest on a double-headed imperial eagle, between the Pillars of Hercules and the motto PLUS ULTRA.
textes.Franco rétablit l'aigle de Saint-Jean, l: Franco restored the eagle of Saint John, the Pillars of Hercules, the yoke and the sheaf of arrows of the Catholic Monarchs.
textes.Les colonnes d'Hercule, anciens noms du: The Pillars of Hercules, an old name for the Strait of Gibraltar, bear the motto PLUS ULTRA, “further beyond”.
textes.Le lion du berceau argovien, que la mais: The lion of the Aargau cradle, which the house would keep at the heart of its arms until the 20th century.
textes.La seule figure trouvée sur Commons est: The only figure found on Commons is filed among “attributed” arms: the shield stays empty.
textes.Les armes des ducs d'Autriche, reprises: The arms of the Dukes of Austria, taken over from the Babenbergs: the white “bind” on red.
textes.Albert II, roi des Romains: Albert II, King of the Romans
textes.Frédéric V d'Autriche, empereur sous le: Frederick V of Austria, Emperor as Frederick III, bore the double-headed imperial eagle.
textes.Adelbrecht et Heralder, écusson de Katep: Adelbrecht and Heralder, escutcheon by Katepanomegas
textes.L'armorial résume ces armes par « De l'E: The armorial sums up these arms as “The Empire, overall: (the preceding arms)”.
textes.Ferdinand, roi de Bohême et de Hongrie: Ferdinand, King of Bohemia and Hungary
textes.Selon l'armorial, Maximilien II puis Jos: According to the armorial, Maximilian II then Joseph I bore the same arms.
textes.Selon l'armorial, Matthias, Ferdinand II: According to the armorial, Matthias, Ferdinand II and Leopold I bore the same arms.
textes.Les armes de l'archiduc Charles avant 17: The arms of Archduke Charles before 1711, when he was disputing Spain with the grandson of Louis XIV.
textes.Adelbrecht et Heralder, éléments de Soda: Adelbrecht and Heralder, elements by Sodacan
textes.Le blasonnement de l'armorial ne porte p: The armorial's blazon does not include the eagle; the Commons figures, titled “empress”, show it. The figure of the shield gives her middle arms, more heavily charged than this blazon.
textes.Le premier Habsbourg-Lorraine : les alér: The first Habsburg-Lorraine: his father's alerions enter at the centre.
textes.Le blasonnement est celui que l'armorial: The blazon is the one the armorial gives for the “lesser arms” of the Emperors of Austria; the figure, of the arms of State, adds crown and collars.
textes.Armes moyennes de l'empire, en usage jus: Middle arms of the empire, in use until 1915 for Austria-Hungary too, according to the file description.
textes.En 1915, le Bindenschild redevient l'emb: In 1915 the Bindenschild became the emblem of Austria again.
textes.Philippe le Beau, roi de Castille: Philip the Handsome, King of Castile
textes.La version de 1530, que l'armorial prése: The 1530 version, which the armorial presents as a simplification of the earlier ones.
textes.Les armes de Philippe époux de Marie Tud: The arms of Philip as husband of Mary Tudor.
textes.Philippe II, roi des Espagnes: Philip II, King of the Spains
textes.Les armes de 1580 sans l'écu de Portugal: The arms of 1580 without the shield of Portugal.
textes.Dates : « Liste des souverains d'Autrich: Dates: “Liste des souverains d'Autriche” and “Liste des monarques d'Espagne”, on Wikipedia. Co-dukes and the Leopoldine and Albertine branches are not shown: the timeline follows the main line of the list.
textes.Armoiries : « Armorial des Habsbourg » p: Arms: “Armorial des Habsbourg” for the blazons, abridged here by naming the quarters (Bohemia, Hungary, Castile…); German and English articles for modern Austria.
textes.Quand les sources divergent, la frise do: When the sources differ, the timeline gives the versions side by side without deciding.
textes.Les écus viennent de Wikimedia Commons,: The shields come from Wikimedia Commons, each with its author and licence checked on its page. Files that Commons files among “disputed” or “attributed” arms have been set aside: their shields stay empty. The collar on the token is drawn by the encyclopedia:
textes.Du lion des comtes argoviens à l'aigle b: From the lion of the Counts in Aargau to the double-headed eagle, six centuries of arms: the Bindenschild at the heart, the kingdoms around it.
textes.duc d'Autriche, puis roi des Romains: Duke of Austria, then King of the Romans
textes.duc d'Autriche, roi de Bohême et de Hong: Duke of Austria, King of Bohemia and Hungary, King of the Romans (Albert II)
textes.archiduc d'Autriche, roi des Romains: Archduke of Austria, King of the Romans
textes.archiduchesse d'Autriche, reine de Bohêm: Archduchess of Austria, Queen of Bohemia and Hungary
textes.empereur élu, puis empereur d'Autriche e: Emperor-elect, then Emperor of Austria in 1804
textes.empereur d'Autriche, roi de Hongrie: Emperor of Austria, King of Hungary
textes.Ladislas, fils posthume d'Albert V, naît: Ladislaus, posthumous son of Albert V, was born in 1440; the list has Frederick V reign from that year.
textes.Rodolphe Iᵉʳ investit ses fils du duché: Rudolf I invested his sons with the Duchy of Austria: the Habsburgs took over the Bindenschild, attested since a seal of 1230.
textes.Albert V, élu roi des Romains, place les: Albert V, elected King of the Romans, placed the arms of his kingdoms on the eagle of the Empire.
textes.Maximilien épouse Marie de Bourgogne : l: Maximilian married Mary of Burgundy: the Burgundian quarters entered his arms.
textes.Ferdinand Iᵉʳ passe de l'écartelé de Boh: Ferdinand I moved from the quartering of Bohemia and Hungary to the double-headed eagle.
textes.L'archiduc Charles, qui disputait l'Espa: Archduke Charles, who had been disputing Spain, became Emperor and set his arms on the eagle.
textes.Avec Joseph II, fils de François de Lorr: With Joseph II, son of Francis of Lorraine, the alerions of Lorraine entered at the centre.
textes.François II fonde l'empire d'Autriche et: Francis II founded the Austrian Empire and took its double-headed eagle.
textes.Fin du Saint-Empire: End of the Holy Roman Empire
textes.Le Saint-Empire est dissous ; l'aigle re: The Holy Roman Empire was dissolved; the eagle remained that of Austria.
textes.L'aigle bicéphale représente l'Autriche: The double-headed eagle represented Austria in the arms of the Dual Monarchy until 1918.
textes.Le Bindenschild redevient l'emblème de l: The Bindenschild became the emblem of Austria again.
textes.La république adopte en 1919 une aigle à: In 1919 the republic adopted a single-headed eagle charged with the Bindenschild.
textes.Grandes armes de Rodolphe II, Matthias e: Great arms of Rudolf II, Matthias and Ferdinand II
textes.Tom Lemmens et Heralder, éléments de Sod: Tom Lemmens and Heralder, elements by Sodacan
textes.Grandes armes de Léopold II et François: Great arms of Leopold II and Francis II
textes.François II, empereur élu et empereur d': Francis II, Emperor-elect and Emperor of Austria
textes.Castille, Aragon, Grenade, Bourgogne, Au: Castile, Aragon, Granada, Burgundy, Austria, then Portugal: the shield of the Kings of Spain of the House of Austria.
textes.Devise personnelle du souverain, en fran: The sovereign's personal motto, in French; it wraps around the pillars, rendered in Latin as “Plus ultra”.
textes.roi des Espagnes, roi de Portugal en 158: King of the Spains, King of Portugal in 1580
textes.roi des Espagnes et de Portugal: King of the Spains and of Portugal
textes.Roi de Portugal jusqu'en 1640, date à la: King of Portugal until 1640, when the armorial removes the shield of Portugal from him; the Commons file keeps it until 1668.
textes.La reine Jeanne, veuve de Philippe le Be: Queen Joanna, widow of Philip the Handsome, was not a Habsburg; Charles reigned after her, with her in Castile until her death in 1555.
textes.Charles réunit les quartiers d'Espagne e: Charles brought together the quarters of Spain and those of his Burgundian and Austrian inheritance.
textes.Couronné empereur, Charles pose ses arme: Crowned Emperor, Charles set his arms of Spain on the eagle, between the Pillars of Hercules.
textes.Philippe II devient roi de Portugal ; l': Philip II became King of Portugal; the shield of Portugal entered over the Spanish quarters.
textes.Le Portugal se soulève et se donne un ro: Portugal rose up and gave itself a king.
textes.L'armorial retire l'écu de Portugal dès: The armorial removes the shield of Portugal from 1640; the Commons files keep it until 1668.
textes.Charles II meurt sans enfant ; la guerre: Charles II died childless; the War of the Spanish Succession began.
textes.Charles Quint : l'aigle, les colonnes et: Charles V: the eagle, the pillars and the Golden Fleece
textes.Les armes de Charles Quint s'entourent d: The arms of Charles V were surrounded by the collar of the Order of the Golden Fleece.
textes.L'héraldique n'existe pas encore. Des ar: Heraldry does not exist yet. Arms would be credited to these popes much later: the first collections of the imaginary heraldry of the popes appeared around the time of the Council of Trent, and Pierre Palliot was still creating them in the 17th century. For lack of a free figure for these invented arms, the timeline does not draw them.
textes.Pendant la vacance du Siège, l'emblème d: During the vacancy of the See, the emblem of the Holy See replaces the pope's arms: the pavilion (ombrellino) above the keys in saltire.
textes.Gravure ancienne d'armes de fantaisie («: Old engraving of fanciful arms (“Phantasiewappen”) credited to Gregory the Great, who died five centuries before the birth of heraldry.
textes.Gravure ancienne (XIXᵉ siècle ou avant): Old engraving (19th century or earlier): these arms were credited to the pope after the fact. No witness from his lifetime shows them.
textes.gravure ancienne (XIXᵉ s. ou avant), aut: old engraving (19th c. or earlier), unknown author
textes.Armes des Conti di Segni: Arms of the Conti di Segni
textes.ou d'argent chapé de sable (qui sont les: or argent, chapé sable (the old arms of the Dominican Order).
textes.Armes des Roger de Beaufort: Arms of the Roger de Beaufort
textes.Commons classe ce dessin parmi les armoi: Commons files this drawing among disputed arms: the roses are seeded in it, a reading judged mistaken.
textes.John Woodward, d'après Echando una mano: John Woodward, after Echando una mano
textes.Armes parlantes : entre la famille Cervi: Canting arms: on the family name Cervini and the stag (cervo).
textes.Armes parlantes : entre la famille Casta: Canting arms: on the family name Castagna and the chestnut tree. Bendy gules and or, on a chief gules a chestnut leaf or, supported by a fess argent.
