Per pale: 1, argent, a patriarchal cross sable on a mount vert, with the three letters PAX sable overall; 2, per bend or and azure, on a bend argent three Moor's heads sable, wreathed argent, on a chief azure three stars or ill-ordered.
textes.Armes parlantes : En italien, chiesa sig: Canting arms: in Italian, chiesa means church.
textes.Armes parlantes : entre la colombe de la: Canting arms: on the dove of peace and Pacelli (pace means peace in Italian).
textes.Écu non plus « en calice » mais à « tête: The shield is no longer “chalice-shaped” but “horse-head”.
textes.Armes parlantes : entre monte (mont en i: Canting arms: on monte (Italian for mount) and Montini.
textes.Le blason est de type « écu à calice »,: The arms are of the “chalice” shield type, chapé and lowered. These three symbols (escallop, bear, Moor's head) are symbols of Bavaria and the Archdiocese of Munich and already appeared in the episcopal arms of Joseph Ratzinger when he was Archbishop of Munich. The two chapes are the symbol of monastic spirituality (in Joseph Ratzinger's case, Benedictine spirituality).
textes.Le meuble assez complexe qui figure en c: The rather complex charge in chief is the seal of the Jesuit order. Unlike the arms of other popes of the modern era, Francis had his motto shown explicitly beneath.
textes.Le meuble qui figure en senestre est ins: The charge on the sinister side is inspired by the symbols of the Order of Saint Augustine. Leo XIV chose to show his motto beneath the shield, like Francis.
textes.L'article « Armoiries papales » blasonne: The article “Armoiries papales” blazons a pierced cross azure; Bouyé recognises in a drawing from his pontificate the “five points equipollent” of Geneva, his house.
textes.Armes parlantes : la lune pour Pedro de: Canting arms: the moon (luna) for Pedro de Luna.
textes.Ni l'article « Armoiries papales », ni l: Neither the article “Armoiries papales”, nor the Spanish, Catalan, Italian and English articles on the antipope, nor the Commons page for the file blazon these arms: only the figure is reproduced.
textes.Deux mille ans de pontificats. Les premi: Two thousand years of pontificates. The first popes had no arms: heraldry was born in the 12th century, and the shields credited to them were invented after the fact. Those are marked “a posteriori”. True papal arms — a family's shield under the keys and tiara — appear only at the end of the 13th century.
textes.Entre deux pontificats, le Siège est vac: Between two pontificates, the See is vacant: the emblem of the Holy See — the pavilion over the keys in saltire — replaces the pope's arms.
textes.Avant les armoiries, les actes pontifica: Before arms, papal acts were authenticated by a lead bulla in the pope's name.
textes.Dates des pontificats : « Liste des pape: Dates of pontificates: “Liste des papes” on Wikipedia. For the early centuries these are traditional dates, often uncertain; the timeline shows them as the list gives them. “Ephemeral” popes and antipopes are set apart, with their arms where they exist.
textes.Armoiries attestées ou non : l'article d: Whether arms are attested or not: the article by Édouard Bouyé (2003), read in full, serves as the guide. Before Nicholas III (1277) and for the four pontificates after him, the arms shown are retrospective: they are marked “a posteriori”. Before 1045, no free figure of these invented arms was found: the timeline does not draw them.
textes.Blasonnements : article « Armoiries papa: Blazons: article “Armoiries papales” on Wikipedia, which refers to Héraldique vaticane and to Neubecker. Eras: sections of the English article “History of the papacy”; its unnamed gaps (752-756, 857-904, 1689-1775) are filled from the divisions of the French article “Histoire de la papauté” (Frankish papacy until 867, Roman barons from 867, Baroque papacy until 1700, Age of Enlightenment). When the sources differ — the first armigerous pope, the second and third crowns of the tiara, the arms of Clement VII of Avignon, the motto of Paul VI — the timeline gives the versions side by side.
textes.Aucune armoirie de son temps : la gravur: No arms from his time: the engraving shown here credits him after the fact with “fanciful arms”.
textes.14 avril 911 ou septembre 911 – juin 913: 14 April 911 or September 911 – June 913 or September 913
textes.Friedrich von Lothringen (Frédéric de Lo: Friedrich von Lothringen (Frederick of Lorraine or of Ardenne)
textes.Eudes (ou Odon) de Lagery (ou de Châtill: Eudes (or Odon) de Lagery (or de Châtillon)
textes.Sous son pontificat, les clés de saint P: During his pontificate, the keys of Saint Peter became detached from the apostle's effigy and turned into the emblem of the Church, on its banner. The Conti arms were credited to him only later.
textes.Désaccord : l'article « Armoiries papale: Disagreement: the article “Armoiries papales” makes him perhaps the first pope with personal arms; Bouyé sees only fanciful shields drawn in the margins of one of his books, and concludes that nothing proves personal use.
textes.Un chroniqueur florentin des années 1340: A Florentine chronicler of the 1340s, Villani, reports that he granted his arms to his Guelph supporters: late testimony, with no monument from his lifetime.
textes.Premier pape attesté à faire usage des a: First pope attested as using his family's arms (palace at Viterbo, frieze on the Capitol, Cimabue's fresco at Assisi): a bare shield, with no keys or tiara.
textes.Simon de Brie ou de Brion: Simon de Brie or de Brion
textes.Son tombeau armorié de l'Ara Coeli, long: His armorial tomb at Ara Coeli, long taken as proof, was set up after 1297 by his brother Pandolfo.
textes.Des armes ne lui sont attribuées qu'à pa: Arms were attributed to him only from the 15th century.
textes.Premier usage systématique : son tombeau: First systematic use: his tomb, consecrated in 1296 during his lifetime, bears three shields or, two bends wavy azure; he was the first to bring his shield together with the keys, tiara and pavilion.
textes.La formule héraldique esquissée sous Bon: The heraldic formula sketched under Boniface VIII became fixed during his pontificate.
textes.Alfons de Borja i de Llançol (Borgia en: Alfons de Borja i de Llançol (Borgia in Italian)
textes.Roderic Llançol i de Borja (Borgia en it: Roderic Llançol i de Borja (Borgia in Italian)
textes.Au nom du Seigneur: In the name of the Lord
textes.La « Liste des papes » donne « Cum ipso: The “Liste des papes” gives “Cum ipso in monte”; the article “Paul VI” gives “In nomine Domini”.
textes.Dernier pape couronné de la tiare, à laq: Last pope crowned with the tiara, which he gave up on 13 November 1964; it remains in the arms of the Holy See.
textes.Premier pape à remplacer la tiare par un: First pope to replace the tiara with a mitre in his arms (three gold bands recalling the three crowns) and to place the pallium beneath the shield. A version with a tiara also appears on his banner from October 2010.
textes.Garde la mitre de son prédécesseur et in: Kept his predecessor's mitre and inscribed his motto beneath the shield.
textes.Inscrite sous l'écu, comme chez François: Inscribed beneath the shield, as with Francis.
textes.Garde la mitre à trois bandes et, comme: Kept the mitre with three bands and, like Francis, inscribed his motto beneath the shield.
textes.Amédée VIII, duc de Savoie, élu par le c: Amadeus VIII, Duke of Savoy, elected by the Council of Basel; he gave up in 1449.
textes.Près de trois ans sans pape : l'article: Nearly three years without a pope: the article “Armoiries papales” marks this vacancy with the emblem of the sede vacante.
textes.Plus de deux ans de vacance, close par l: More than two years of vacancy, closed by the election of Celestine V.
textes.Plus de deux ans de vacance entre Clémen: More than two years of vacancy between Clement V and John XXII.
textes.Après la renonciation de Grégoire XII et: After the renunciation of Gregory XII and the deposition of the antipope John XXIII, the Council of Constance elected Martin V in November 1417 and ended the Western Schism.
textes.La chancellerie pontificale scelle ses a: The papal chancery sealed its acts with a lead bulla in the pope's name — the pope's identity lay in the seal, not in a shield.
textes.Le même article cite, d'après un diction: The same article cites, from a dictionary of 1930, older bullae, as early as Leo I (440-461).
textes.Pépin le Bref remet au pape de larges te: Pepin the Short handed the pope wide territories in central Italy: the birth of the Papal States, which lasted until 1870.
textes.Sous Innocent III, les clés quittent la: Under Innocent III, the keys left the hand of Saint Peter to become the emblem of the Church, on its banner — not yet the arms of a pope.
textes.Nicolas III Orsini est le premier pape a: Nicholas III Orsini is the first pope attested as using his family's arms, on a bare shield.
textes.Boniface VIII fait graver ses armes sur: Boniface VIII had his arms carved on his tomb during his lifetime and combined them with the keys, tiara and pavilion: the formula of papal arms was born.
textes.La plupart des historiens attribuent à B: Most historians credit Boniface VIII with adding a second crown to the tiara.
textes.D'autres en doutent, jugeant l'idée d'un: Others doubt it, judging the idea of a double power contrary to his doctrine.
textes.Les papes s'installent à Avignon, où sep: The popes settled in Avignon, where seven French popes resided until 1377.
textes.Benoît XII fait ajouter une troisième co: Benedict XII had a third crown added to the tiara, shortly before his death.
textes.Selon d'autres historiens, ce serait Jea: According to other historians, it was John XXII, or even Urban V.
textes.Des cardinaux élisent Robert de Genève (: Cardinals elected Robert of Geneva (Clement VII) against Urban VI: two, then three rival obediences, each with its arms.
textes.Le concile de Constance élit Martin V (C: The Council of Constance elected Martin V (Colonna).
textes.L'héraldique imaginaire des papes: The imaginary heraldry of the popes
textes.Vers le concile de Trente paraissent les: Around the Council of Trent appeared the first collections of arms invented for popes earlier than heraldry; this tradition still weighs on recent publications.
textes.Le généalogiste Pierre Palliot codifie l: The genealogist Pierre Palliot codified papal blazon and created arms for popes who bore none, notably before Innocent III.
textes.Rome est prise par l'Italie ; les États: Rome was taken by Italy; the Papal States disappeared and the pope regarded himself as a prisoner in the Vatican.
textes.Les accords du Latran créent l'État de l: The Lateran Treaty created the State of Vatican City.
textes.Paul VI renonce à porter la tiare ; elle: Paul VI gave up wearing the tiara; it remains in the arms of the Holy See.
textes.Benoît XVI met une mitre à trois bandes: Benedict XVI set a mitre with three bands above his shield and the pallium beneath it.
textes.François inscrit sa devise sous ses arme: Francis inscribed his motto beneath his arms; Leo XIV did the same in 2025.
textes.L'héraldique n'existe pas encore. Les ar: Heraldry does not exist yet. The arms shown for these popes would be invented after the fact, from the 16th century.
textes.L'Église se dote d'armes — les clés — ma: The Church acquired arms — the keys — but the popes did not yet display their family's arms: those given to them are retrospective.
textes.Nicolas III use des armes Orsini, sans o: Nicholas III used the Orsini arms, with no outer ornament.
textes.Les quatre pontificats suivants n'ont la: The next four pontificates left no heraldic witness of their time.
textes.L'écu familial du pape, sous les clés et: The pope's family shield, under the keys and tiara: Boniface VIII was the first to use it systematically, and the formula became fixed under John XXII.
textes.Les clés sont l'attribut de saint Pierre: The keys are the attribute of Saint Peter, held in his hand; they are not yet an emblem of the Church.
textes.Détachées de l'apôtre, les clés devienne: Detached from the apostle, the keys became the emblem and then the arms of the Church, on the papal banner.
textes.Posées en sautoir, liées d'un cordon de: Set in saltire, tied with a cord gules: the one in bend is gold, the one in bend sinister silver.
textes.Boniface VIII place la tiare au-dessus d: Boniface VIII placed the tiara above his arms; the second crown is attributed to him around 1301, without certainty.
textes.Trois couronnes à partir de 1342 selon l: Three crowns from 1342 according to the most widespread hypothesis (Benedict XII); others date it to John XXII or Urban V.
textes.Benoît XVI remplace la tiare par la mitr: Benedict XVI replaced the tiara with the mitre; Francis then Leo XIV kept it.
textes.Benoît XVI place sous son blason le pall: Benedict XVI placed the pallium beneath his arms, a sign of collegiality with archbishops and bishops.
textes.François puis Léon XIV inscrivent leur d: Francis then Leo XIV inscribed their mottoes beneath the shield.
textes.La croix d'azur de l'origine aurait perd: The original cross azure is said to have lost its arms; only five shields remained, charged with bezants (from four to eleven depending on the image). This is the oldest verifiable form: probably introduced under Alfonso I, certainly borne under Sancho I. One legend sees in it the five Moorish kings defeated at Ourique, another the five wounds of Christ.
textes.Alphonse III, cadet, ajoute une bordure: Alfonso III, a younger son, added a bordure gules charged with castles or to his father's arms when he pressed his rights against his brother Sancho II, and kept it on becoming king. According to the most widespread hypothesis, it is a cadet's difference, the castles borrowed from the arms of his mother Urraca of Castile; tradition sees in them the last castles taken from the Moors in the Algarve. Their number varies from eight to fourteen.
textes.Béatrice, reine de Castille et de Portug: Beatrice, Queen of Castile and Portugal
textes.Pendant la crise de 1383-1385, Béatrice: During the crisis of 1383-1385, Beatrice bore the arms of Portugal in the 2nd and 3rd quarters, with those of her husband in the 1st and 4th.
textes.Jean Iᵉʳ, grand maître de l'ordre d'Aviz: John I, Grand Master of the Order of Aviz, added the cross of his order: sometimes in the bordure, between the castles, more often in the shield, sometimes outside the shield, set upon it.
textes.Alphonse V réclame la couronne de Castil: Alfonso V claimed the crown of Castile from 1475 to 1479: his arms bear Portugal in the 1st and 4th quarters, Castile and León in the 2nd and 3rd.
textes.En 1485, Jean II fait corriger ce qu'il: In 1485 John II had corrected what he regarded as errors: the cross of Aviz disappeared, the dexter and sinister shields were set upright (lying down, they might have been taken for a mark of bastardy) and the bezants were fixed at five in saltire, for the five wounds of Christ, his devotion. The group of five shields with five bezants is called the “quinas”, a name later given to the whole shield. The castles of the bordure were fixed at seven under Sebastian. The composition no longer changes after that (except the armillary sphere of 1815-1826); until 1910, the colours and drawing of the castles vary with the artist.
textes.Prêtre, Henri fait ajouter à la couronne: A priest, Henry had the red hat and tassels of his rank as cardinal added to the royal crown: a composition unique to his reign.
textes.Quand le Brésil devient un royaume à par: When Brazil became a kingdom in its own right within the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves (1815), the shield of Portugal (for Portugal and the Algarves) was set on the armillary sphere or on a field azure (for Brazil). These arms served from 1815 to 1826: Brazil was independent from 1822, but Portugal went back to the old arms only on the death of John VI.
textes.D'une croix d'azur aux cinq écus d'Alpho: From a cross azure to the five shields of Alfonso I, to the bordure of Castile, then the cross of Aviz and the quinas fixed in 1485: seven centuries for a single shield, which hardly moves afterwards, except for the armillary sphere of Brazil.
textes.Dates des règnes : « Liste des rois et r: Dates of reigns: “Liste des rois et reines de Portugal” (Wikipedia), which gives years; precise dates (death of Ferdinand, Peter IV, death of Charles I, fall of the monarchy) come from the same list and the article “Pierre Ier (empereur du Brésil)”. Regencies and the period 1383-1385 are noted there. António, Prior of Crato, whom the list sets apart and most historians regard as a mere claimant, has his row “On the margins”.
textes.Armoiries : « Coat of arms of Portugal »: Arms: “Coat of arms of Portugal” (English Wikipedia) for the whole history of the shield, charges, crests, supporters and crowns. Where the article contradicts itself (1481 or 1485 for the corrected version of the shield; 1247 or 1248 for the accession of Alfonso III), the timeline gives both dates.
textes.Louis-Philippe, fils aîné de Charles Iᵉʳ: Louis Philippe, eldest son of Charles I, who died twenty minutes after him and was never proclaimed king, is not shown. The Habsburg kings of 1580 to 1640 are in Portugal for their shield of Portugal; their full arms are in the Habsburg timeline.
textes.Premier roi, d'abord comte puis duc : le: First king, at first count then duke: the kingdom proclaimed itself in 1139 and was recognised in 1143. The exact form of his arms remains uncertain.
textes.Déclaré « rex innutilis » et destitué pa: Declared “rex innutilis” and deposed by Pope Innocent IV at the Council of Lyon in 1245, he abdicated in 1247, went into exile in Toledo and died at the start of 1248. His brother Alfonso, Count of Boulogne, served as regent from 1245.
textes.Régent depuis 1245, il monte sur le trôn: Regent since 1245, he came to the throne on his brother's death. The English article dates his accession to 1247.
textes.Seule fille de Ferdinand, mariée à Jean: Only daughter of Ferdinand, married to John I of Castile. The list does not number her: her mother held the regency, and the aristocracy, fearing Castilian influence, set off the crisis of 1383-1385.
textes.Fils illégitime de Pierre Iᵉʳ et grand m: Illegitimate son of Peter I and Grand Master of the Order of Aviz, first king of his house, with the longest reign in Portuguese history. From at least his reign, the crest is a dragon, probably linked to the choice of Saint George as patron of the kingdom.
textes.Il monte sur le trône à six ans (régence: He came to the throne at six (regencies of Eleanor of Aragon, then of Peter of Coimbra).
textes.Il fait « corriger » l'écu en 1485 : ce: He had the shield “corrected” in 1485: these are the quinas.
textes.Sa sphère armillaire, emblème personnel,: His armillary sphere, a personal emblem, and the cross of the Order of Christ, of which he was Grand Master, henceforth surround the shield; they would become national insignia.
textes.Les châteaux de la bordure sont fixés à: The castles of the bordure were fixed at seven; the open crown became closed, with one arch. He died at the Battle of Ksar el-Kebir.
textes.Cardinal, il ne peut avoir d'héritier lé: A cardinal, he could not have a legitimate heir: Pope Gregory XIII refused to release him from orders.
textes.Les armes de la maison de Habsbourg port: The arms of the House of Habsburg bear the shield of Portugal at the honour point, but this quartering serves only to represent the King personally: in the kingdom, the shield of Portugal alone is kept.
textes.Le modèle définitif de la couronne royal: The final model of the royal crown, closed with four arches, was adopted in his reign.
textes.Elle partage le pouvoir avec son oncle e: She shared power with her uncle and husband Peter III, king jure uxoris from 1777 to 1786. Mentally unstable, she fled to Brazil before Junot; the regency was held by her son John.
textes.Il fuit au Brésil avec sa mère et la fam: He fled to Brazil with his mother and the royal family; the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves was proclaimed in 1815.
textes.Empereur du Brésil, il abdique le 2 mai: Emperor of Brazil, he abdicated on 2 May 1826 in favour of his daughter Maria.
textes.Renversée par son oncle Michel, qui pren: Overthrown by her uncle Miguel, who took power; Miguel's regency began in 1827.
textes.Son court règne est marqué par une guerr: His short reign was marked by a civil war that ended with his removal and the restoration of Maria II.
textes.Son mariage avec Ferdinand de Saxe-Cobou: Her marriage to Ferdinand of Saxe-Coburg-Gotha in effect ended the reign of the House of Braganza. Ferdinand II was king jure uxoris from 1837 to 1853.
textes.Assassiné avec son fils aîné Louis-Phili: Assassinated with his eldest son Louis Philippe, who survived him by about twenty minutes but was never proclaimed king: the list does not count him.
textes.Renversé par la révolution de 1910, il s: Overthrown by the revolution of 1910, he went into exile in the United Kingdom. The republic had the shield redrawn, and its colours and the drawing of the castles were then fixed.
textes.La crise de 1383-1385 : Jean, grand maît: The crisis of 1383-1385: John, Grand Master of the Order of Aviz, was regent from 16 December 1383 until his acclamation as king in 1385.
textes.Petit-fils de Manuel Iᵉʳ, regardé par un: Grandson of Manuel I, regarded by a small minority of historians as king: most see only a claimant defeated by Philip II of Spain at Alcántara. The list gives him a month's reign.
textes.Un royaume sans écu sûr: A kingdom with no certain shield
textes.Alphonse Iᵉʳ se proclame roi, et le roya: Alfonso I proclaimed himself king, and the kingdom was recognised in 1143. His shield is thought to have been argent, a cross azure; the bezants are said to have been added after recognition.
textes.La plus ancienne forme vérifiable de l'é: The oldest verifiable form of the shield, with five shields, is that of his successor Sancho I.
textes.Sous Sanche Iᵉʳ, l'écu est sûrement form: Under Sancho I, the shield was certainly made up of five shields azure charged with bezants.
textes.Alphonse III monte sur le trône avec les: Alfonso III came to the throne with the arms he had taken as a younger son: the shield of Portugal surrounded by a bordure gules with castles or, borrowed from his Castilian mother.
textes.L'article anglais date son avènement de: The English article dates his accession to 1247; the French list, to 1248.
textes.Jean d'Aviz, acclamé roi, ajoute à l'écu: John of Aviz, acclaimed king, added the cross of his order to the shield.
textes.Alphonse V réclame la Castille de 1475 à: Alfonso V claimed Castile from 1475 to 1479 and quartered his arms with those of Castile and León.
textes.Jean II fait corriger l'écu : la croix d: John II had the shield corrected: the cross of Aviz disappeared, the shields were set upright, five bezants in saltire.
textes.Dans sa galerie, l'article anglais date: In its gallery, the English article dates the corrected version to 1481; in its text, to 1485.
textes.Sous Sébastien, les châteaux de la bordu: Under Sebastian, the castles of the bordure were fixed at seven and the open crown gave way to a crown closed with one arch.
textes.Philippe II d'Espagne, devenu roi de Por: Philip II of Spain, having become King of Portugal, placed the shield of Portugal at the honour point of his arms. In Portugal itself, the shield alone is kept.
textes.Avec les Bragance, dont la livrée est ve: With the Braganzas, whose livery is green, the dragon of the crest went from gold to green: green became the national colour.
textes.L'article anglais le dit « probable » :: The English article calls this “probable”: it is an explanation, not an established fact.
textes.Le Brésil est élevé au rang de royaume :: Brazil was raised to a kingdom: the shield of Portugal was set on the armillary sphere or on a field azure, the arms of Brazil.
textes.À la mort de Jean VI, le Portugal repren: On the death of John VI, Portugal took back the shield without the armillary sphere, although Brazil had been independent since 1822.
textes.Manuel II est renversé le 5 octobre 1910: Manuel II was overthrown on 5 October 1910; the republic kept the shield, but fixed its colours and the drawing of its castles.
textes.Supports : deux anges, qui tiennent l'éc: Supporters: two angels, holding the shield (from the drawing in the file)
textes.Couronne royale au-dessus de l'écu (d'ap: Royal crown above the shield (from the drawing)
textes.L'article donne les anges pour supports: The article gives angels as the usual supporters of the shield until the 18th century, and cites this 15th-century model (House of Aviz); the file does not date it more precisely.
textes.Philippe Iᵉʳ : l'écu avec ses ornements: Philip I: the shield with its ornaments
textes.Heaume d'or, couronne et dragon en cimie: Golden helm, crown and dragon as crest (from the drawing in the file)
textes.Mantelage aux couleurs de l'écu (d'après: Mantling in the colours of the shield (from the drawing)
textes.D'après la page de titre d'un recueil de: After the title page of a collection of privileges of 1583.
textes.Les Bragance : écu, dragons et bannières: The Braganzas: shield, dragons and banners
textes.Supports : deux dragons de sinople porta: Supporters: two dragons vert bearing, to dexter, a banner argent with the five shields; to sinister, a banner gules with the seven castles or
textes.Le fichier couvre 1640-1910 sans disting: The file covers 1640-1910 without distinguishing periods; according to the article, green dragons became the usual supporter only in the 18th century.
textes.fermée, à une puis deux arches: closed, with one then two arches
textes.Sous Sébastien, la couronne ouverte devi: Under Sebastian, the open crown became closed, with one arch; it later evolved into a crown with two arches.
textes.Le modèle définitif est adopté sous Pier: The final model was adopted under Peter II: a crown closed with four arches, surmounted by an orb and cross. The crown with two arches became that of the crown prince.
textes.À partir de Jean Iᵉʳ au moins, le cimier: From at least John I, the crest is a dragon, probably linked to the choice of Saint George as patron of Portugal. Until the 17th century, it is gold.
textes.Le dragon devient vert, sans doute avec: The dragon became green, probably with the accession of the Braganzas, whose livery is green.
textes.Jusqu'au XVIIIᵉ siècle, les supports les: Until the 18th century, the most frequent supporters are two angels, sometimes just one; the article cites those of the House of Aviz in the 15th century. From Manuel I they are seen handling armillary spheres and crosses of the Order of Christ.
textes.À partir du XVIIIᵉ siècle, les dragons v: From the 18th century, the green dragons of the crest also became the usual supporters, each bearing a banner: the argent one with the five shields to dexter, the gules one with the seven castles to sinister.
textes.sphère armillaire et croix du Christ: armillary sphere and cross of Christ
textes.Sous Manuel Iᵉʳ, son emblème personnel (: Under Manuel I, his personal emblem (the armillary sphere) and the cross of the Order of Christ, of which he was Grand Master, often surround the shield; they would move from personal emblem to national symbol.
textes.La sphère armillaire d'or sur azur, arme: The armillary sphere or on azure, the arms of Brazil, supports the shield of Portugal.
textes.Dans la seconde moitié du XIXᵉ siècle, l: In the second half of the 19th century, the shield is often covered by a purple pavilion lined with ermine, emerging from the crown.
textes.Jusque vers 1200, les rares documents ne: Until about 1200, the few documents mention no banner or insignia particular to the descendants of Humbert: at this time, the use of arms is not yet fixed.
textes.Première insigne documentée, prise en 12: First documented insignia, taken in 1217 by Thomas I: a black single-headed eagle, wings displayed and inverted, “probably” on a field or. This is the emblem of the Empire, of which the Count is vicar.
textes.La croix blanche sur champ rouge : le se: The white cross on a red field: the one element that runs through all Savoyard arms since the Middle Ages.
textes.Philippe Ier revient à l'aigle noire, dé: Philip I went back to the black eagle, now double-headed and on a field argent, like the imperial emblem of his time. No free figure of these arms was found: the shield stays empty.
textes.Emmanuel-Philibert écartèle la croix ave: Emmanuel Philibert quartered the cross with Saxony, Westphalia and Engern — in the name of a legendary Saxon origin of his house — and with Chablais and Aosta.
textes.Victor-Amédée Ier revendique les couronn: Victor Amadeus I claimed the crowns of Cyprus and Jerusalem: their arms (with Lusignan) entered the shield, along with Geneva and Montferrat.
textes.Description d'après l'article italien, q: Description from the Italian article, which gives no complete blazon. The eagle on argent represents the new Kingdom of Sicily.
textes.La Sicile échangée contre la Sardaigne,: Sicily having been exchanged for Sardinia, the arms of Sardinia — the cross between four Moor's heads — entered the shield.
textes.Victor-Emmanuel Ier reçoit Gênes en 1815: Victor Emmanuel I received Genoa in 1815 and took the occasion to simplify his arms: the red cross of Genoa entered them.
textes.L'article français donne le blasonnement: The French article gives the complete blazon, quarter by quarter; it is summarised here. Charles Albert in practice preferred the small shield with the cross alone.
textes.Des comtes de Maurienne aux rois d'Itali: From the Counts of Maurienne to the Kings of Italy, the shield moves from eagle to cross, loads itself with claims — Saxony, Cyprus, Jerusalem, Sicily, Sardinia — then returns in 1848 to the lone cross argent on gules.
textes.Dates des règnes : « Liste des comtes et: Dates of reigns: “Liste des comtes et ducs de Savoie”, “Liste des rois de Sardaigne” and “Liste des rois d'Italie”, on Wikipedia. The dates of the first counts are traditional and often approximate; the timeline shows them as the list gives them. Names link to the French Wikipedia article on the sovereign.
textes.Armoiries : « Armorial de la maison de S: Arms: “Armorial de la maison de Savoie” for the blazons, the Italian article “Simboli degli Stati sabaudi” (after Gerbaix de Sonnaz, 1896) for the beginnings and ornaments, the Italian article “Stemma del Regno d'Italia”, which cites the texts of 1870, 1890 and 1929, for the Kingdom of Italy.
textes.Quand les sources divergent — date de la: When the sources differ — date of the first cross, foundation of the Order of the Collar, year of the shield of Cyprus and Jerusalem, numbering of the Charleses, end of the reign of Humbert II — the timeline gives the versions side by side without deciding.
textes.Couronne et collier des jetons sont dess: The crown and collar on the tokens are drawn by the encyclopedia; the double-headed eagle of Philip I, for lack of a free figure, stays an empty shield. Shields, great arms and arms from before the throne come from Wikimedia Commons, each with its author and licence checked on its page:
textes.Il use encore de l'aigle, mais l'alterne: He still used the eagle, but now alternated it with the white cross on gules.
textes.Avec lui, l'usage de la croix devient dé: With him, the use of the cross became final.
textes.comte, puis premier duc de Savoie: Count, then first Duke of Savoy
textes.Élu pape par le concile de Bâle sous le: Elected pope by the Council of Basel as Felix V, he kept the cross of Savoy as pope.
textes.La liste des ducs l'appelle Charles III: The list of dukes calls him Charles III; his article names him Charles II, the numbering varying depending on whether Charles John Amadeus is counted.
textes.duc de Savoie, roi de Sicile, puis de Sa: Duke of Savoy, King of Sicily, then of Sardinia
textes.L'usage des armes de Savoie lui étant dé: The use of the arms of Savoy being forbidden to him, the Council of the Seal of Titles granted him others; the horse forcené takes up that of Lower Saxony.
textes.roi de Sardaigne, puis d'Italie: King of Sardinia, then of Italy
textes.Son article donne le 18 juin 1946 comme: His article gives 18 June 1946 as the end of the reign; the same article calls him king until 12 June.
textes.Thomas Ier arbore une aigle noire à une: Thomas I displayed a black single-headed eagle, the emblem of the Empire, of which he was vicar in Italy.
textes.Pour l'article français, d'après Bernard: For the French article, after Bernard Demotz, the cross appears as early as 1143 on the pennon of a seal of Amadeus III; the Italian article lists this date among the theses of the old chroniclers.
textes.Pierre II, devenu comte, alterne l'aigle: Peter II, having become count, alternated the eagle and the cross. It is said to come from the emblem of the English crusaders, with whom he had taken the cross in 1250-1251.
textes.Philippe Ier reprend l'aigle noire, déso: Philip I took up the black eagle again, now double-headed and on a field argent.
textes.Sous Amédée V, au XIVᵉ siècle, l'usage d: Under Amadeus V, in the 14th century, the use of the cross became final.
textes.Le comte Édouard adopte le cimier au muf: Count Edward adopted the crest with the winged lion's face, which the dukes would keep.
textes.Amédée VI, le comte Vert, fonde l'ordre: Amadeus VI, the Green Count, founded the Order of the Collar.
textes.La liste des comtes date la fondation de: The list of counts dates the foundation to 1362; the article on the Order retains 1364 and regards 1362 as an error.
textes.L'empereur Sigismond érige le comté en d: Emperor Sigismund raised the county to a duchy. The dukes kept the cross, but cut their banner “in flame” to distinguish it from those of their vassals.
textes.Élu pape par le concile de Bâle sous le: Elected pope by the Council of Basel as Felix V, Amadeus VIII kept the cross of Savoy as pope.
textes.Charles le Bon ajoute au collier l'image: Charles the Good added the image of the Annunciation to the collar: the order became the Supreme Order of the Most Holy Annunziata.
textes.Ses États recouvrés, Emmanuel-Philibert: His States recovered, Emmanuel Philibert quartered the cross with Saxony, Westphalia, Engern, Chablais and Aosta, and surrounded the shield with the collar of the Order.
textes.Victor-Amédée Ier, qui prétend aux couro: Victor Amadeus I, who claimed the crowns of Cyprus and Jerusalem, brought their arms into the shield, with Geneva and Montferrat, and placed it under a pavilion.
textes.L'article français date ce changement de: The French article dates this change to 1630, the Italian article to the end of 1632.
textes.Par les traités d'Utrecht, Victor-Amédée: By the Treaties of Utrecht, Victor Amadeus II became King of Sicily: Nice and Saluzzo entered the shield, and the eagle of Sicily, charged with Savoy, took its centre.
textes.La Sicile échangée contre la Sardaigne,: Sicily having been exchanged for Sardinia, the eagle moved to a field or and the shield of Sardinia with the four Moor's heads was added.
textes.Victor-Emmanuel Ier reçoit Gênes et simp: Victor Emmanuel I received Genoa and simplified his arms; the red cross of Genoa entered them.
textes.Charles-Albert, de la branche de Carigna: Charles Albert, of the Carignano branch, took up the arms of 1720, adding Genoa, Nice, Piedmont and Saluzzo, but in practice preferred the small shield with the cross alone.
textes.Charles-Albert place l'écu de Savoie, bo: Charles Albert placed the shield of Savoy, edged azure, on the tricolour flag; the emblem of State became the crowned shield, surrounded by the collar, with a trophy of flags.
textes.Le nouveau royaume garde les armes d'ori: The new kingdom kept the original arms: gules, a cross argent.
textes.Une délibération de la Consulta araldica: A resolution of the Consulta araldica fixed the ornaments of the shield: crowned helm, orders, lions holding guidons, mantle and pavilion.
textes.Le décret du 27 novembre 1890 supprime m: The decree of 27 November 1890 removed mantle and lances, set the royal crown on the pavilion and placed the Iron Crown on the helm.
textes.Le décret du 11 avril 1929 remplace les: The decree of 11 April 1929 replaced the lions with two lictors' fasces; the motto FERT appears three times.
textes.Le référendum du 2 juin 1946 abolit la m: The referendum of 2 June 1946 abolished the monarchy; the emblem of the Republic would replace the shield of Savoy in 1948.
textes.Les ducs : la croix sous le lion ailé: The dukes: the cross under the winged lion
textes.Cimier : un mufle de lion ailé, en usage: Crest: a winged lion's face, in use since Count Edward (1327)
textes.Le fichier date ces armes de « ~1416 »,: The file dates these arms “~1416”, without further precision.
textes.Trois heaumes : couronne ducale au lion: Three helms: ducal crown with the winged lion, crests of Meissen and Saxony
textes.Victor-Amédée Ier : l'écu sous le pavill: Victor Amadeus I: the shield under the pavilion
textes.Pavillon, d'où sort le fer d'une lance d: Pavilion, from which emerges the head of a tournament lance bearing the banner gules, a cross argent
textes.Emblème de l'État sarde dès 1848, gardé: Emblem of the Sardinian State from 1848, kept by the Kingdom of Italy until 1870.
textes.Colliers et grand-croix des ordres: Collars and grand crosses of the orders
textes.Manteau de pourpre semé de roses et de n: Purple mantle semé of roses and knots of Savoy
textes.Pavillon d'azur sommé d'une étoile d'arg: Pavilion azure topped by a star argent
textes.Heaume royal sommé de la Couronne de fer: Royal helm topped by the Iron Crown
textes.Supports : deux lions, d'or ou au nature: Supporters: two lions, or or proper
textes.Grandes insignes des ordres équestres it: Grand insignia of the Italian equestrian orders
textes.Pavillon royal sommé de la couronne roya: Royal pavilion topped by the royal crown
textes.Gonfalon d'Italie à l'aigle d'or couronn: Gonfalon of Italy with a crowned golden eagle
textes.En 1927, le faisceau de licteur est acco: In 1927 the lictor's fasces was set beside the arms of 1890.
textes.Heaume royal d'or sommé de la Couronne d: Golden royal helm topped by the Iron Crown
textes.Supports : deux faisceaux de licteur lié: Supporters: two lictors' fasces tied with knots of Savoy
textes.Grand collier de l'Annonciade et grandes: Grand collar of the Annunziata and grand sashes of the orders
textes.Pavillon de pourpre sommé de la couronne: Purple pavilion topped by the royal crown
textes.Dès 1848, l'écu de Savoie est sommé de l: From 1848 the shield of Savoy is topped by the royal crown; in 1870 it tops the helm, in 1890 it moves to the pavilion.
textes.Emmanuel-Philibert entoure l'écu du coll: Emmanuel Philibert surrounded the shield with the collar of the Supreme Order; it stayed there until the decrees of 1870, 1890 and 1929.
textes.Emmanuel-Philibert fait soutenir l'écu p: Emmanuel Philibert had the shield held by two golden lions; the sources read do not say until when.
textes.1870 : deux lions tenant des guidons ; 1: 1870: two lions holding guidons; 1890: two lions, or or proper.
